content:
The film company behind the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything,” A24, posted on Instagram that it granted a request from NASA to screen the film on the International Space Station (ISS).

Unless A24 is deceiving us (why would they?), it appears that some astronauts can’t wait to come back to Earth to see the film that everyone’s talking about, which has reached number one at the box office.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

“You Can See Everything,” directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, initially debuted in North America with a limited theatrical rollout. The film has been so successful, though, that it’s generating demand from international audiences.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Sony Pictures acquired the right to release the film in theaters in Germany, Latin America, South Korea, and other territories, though it hasn’t announced its plans yet. The film won’t come out in the U.K. until November 20, while French viewers will have to wait until December 30.

So yes, it is currently easier to watch “You Can See Everything” in low-Earth orbit than in London. These hard-working astronauts can take a break from their complex scientific research to address an equally bewildering question: does Elizabeth Holmes really believe her own lies?

title: Waymo confirms it will split with Uber in January 2028
excerpt: Waymo will officially split with Uber in the Austin and Atlanta markets starting in January 2028, co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg News in a report published Wednesday.
description: Waymo will officially split with Uber in the Austin and Atlanta markets starting in January 2028, co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg News in a report published Wednesday.
content:
Waymo will officially split with Uber in the Austin and Atlanta markets starting in January 2028, co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana told Bloomberg News in a report published Wednesday.

The robotaxi company will instead offer rides directly through its own smartphone app, like it does in other cities. Mawakana’s comments confirm reporting earlier this year by the Financial Times that Waymo was looking to get out of its deal with Uber, which was set to expire in May 2028.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Mawakana told Bloomberg that Waymo initially partnered with Uber because the ride-hail giant offered scale. But the experience for riders has been “a little bit of a crapshoot,” she said, especially because riders never know for sure if they’re going to hail a robotaxi or a human-driven car.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“It’s important for us to have that relationship with the rider. We’ve gotten that feedback from the riders in those markets,” Mawakana said.

Uber — which has many robotaxi and other autonomous vehicle partners — told Bloomberg that it was Waymo’s idea not to add an option in the ride-hail giant’s app to book a robotaxi directly.

Cattini worked with Tom Jones, Dusty Springfield, Tony Christie, Paul Weller and Paul McCartney

Tributes have been paid after the death of drummer Clem Cattini, who performed on several UK Number One singles.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The 89-year-old, who lived in Hertfordshire, co-founded the Tornados in 1961. Their instrumental Telstar spent five weeks at the top of the UK chart in 1962, and they became the first British group to top the US Billboard Hot 100.

As a session musician, he played on number one hits such as Tom Jones' Green, Green Grass of Home, Dusty Springfield's You Don't Have To Say You Love Me and Tony Christie's (Is This the Way to) Amarillo?.

In a Facebook post, external Christie described Cattini as "a world class musician but also a world class gentleman".

He wrote: "So very sad to hear that the great Clem Cattini, drummer of the Tornados and prolific session drummer has passed away. Clem played on more number 1 records than any other British drummer.

"Proud to have known him. My condolences and love to his family."

Carl Palmer, drummer with groups Emerson, Lake & Palmer and Asia, said: "The drummers all over the UK owe you a lot for opening the door for all of us."

The drummer was born to Italian parents in Stoke Newington, north London, in August 1937

North London band The Equals, who topped the charts in 1968 with Baby Come Back, posted on social media, external: "The legendary Clem Cattini, a true powerhouse of percussion and one of the most prolific drummers in British recording history.

"An absolute legend who leaves behind an incredible musical legacy."

Cattini also played on Engelbert Humperdinck's Release Me, Love Affair's Everlasting Love and Johnny Kidd & The Pirates' Shakin' All Over.

Teen musician is flying the flag for the recorder

His other credits included recording with Paul Weller, The Kinks and The Wombles.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He played drums on all 11 tracks of Thrillington, an instrumental reworking of Paul and Linda McCartney's album Ram, which the former Beatle released under the pseudonym Percy "Thrills" Thrillington.

Cattini toured with Cliff Richard and Roy Orbison, and performed on television with the Top Of the Pops orchestra.

He was played by James Corden in the 2008 film Telstar, about Tornados producer Joe Meek.

title: Why Kim Kardashian came back to 'the worst TV drama ever'
excerpt: 'I'm not a quitter': Kim Kardashian on retaking the bar exam
description: 'I'm not a quitter': Kim Kardashian on retaking the bar exam
content:
'I'm not a quitter': Kim Kardashian on retaking the bar exam

It was meant to be Kim Kardashian's triumphant debut as a leading actor - but last year's legal drama All's Fair was so universally panned by critics that it actually broke streaming records as audiences clambered to see what all the fuss was about.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Kardashian, who is best known as a media personality and businesswoman, tells the BBC she had no choice but to "lean into" the discourse and come back for a second series.

"We thought we were this law show, dealing with some really serious issues," she jokes.

But viewers mostly enjoyed its comedy value - with outlandish outfits and zingy one-liners from co-stars Sarah Paulson and Glenn Close sending the show straight into the pantheon of 'camp classics'.

Kim Kardashian has returned to her role as Allura Grant in Ryan Murphy's legal drama All's Fair

"We're a full comedy now," the 46-year-old admits, adding: "The beauty in producing a show with writers that are really tuned in to pop culture is they can see what the response is and write accordingly to that."

All's Fair, which was created by American Horror Story and Glee showrunner Ryan Murphy, became the Hulu network's most-watched scripted series debut of the last three years and was immediately renewed.

Following a group of divorce lawyers - played by Kardashian, Close, Paulson, Naomi Watts and Niecy Nash-Betts - the show was panned for bad acting, with Kardashian bearing the brunt of criticism.

The Hollywood Reporter called her "wooden", and the Times declared that the show "may be the worst TV drama ever".

But the hallmark of Kardashian's career has been her ability to back herself - whether that's going from years of being snubbed by Met Gala organisers to becoming its most anticipated guest, or overcoming backlash to the launch of her shapewear company to turn it into a $5bn (£3.7bn) brand.

Kardashian says: "What is the alternative, right? What is the other choice that you have when you're getting criticised?

"Do you just fall in and feel that, or keep your head down and try better, try harder and try a different path?"

Having been in the spotlight for more than 20 years, she's "always had a really good sense of my mental health", and says that comes from being able to "brush off" those who seek to bring her down.

"I always do things that are tough because I genuinely want to learn," Kardashian says.

Kardashian's co-stars Sarah Paulson and Naomi Watts have also returned for season two

While she was promoting the legal drama last year, Kardashian was waiting to find out if she had passed exams to become a lawyer in real life, after six years of studying for an apprenticeship that negated the need for a university degree.

Shortly after the first series aired, she found out she had failed the exam - but says that won't be the end of her pursuit of the qualification.

"If I don't pass something, if I don't do the best at something, then I'll get there," she says. "I don't worry. I just have to keep going."

But after her admission that she had used AI for legal advice, external, she does say she will change how public she is about her studies.

"I'm going to be a little more quiet about my journey until I get there," says Kardashian, who has four children with rapper Kanye West and is now in a relationship with British Formula 1 driver Lewis Hamilton.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

"I know there was a lot of talk out there like, 'she's given up', and that's funny to me.

"I like people to think what they want to think and I'll take it again and let you guys know once I've passed. I'll be very vocal about that," she says.

All's Fair was criticised in its first series for bad acting, but Kardashian's co-stars say she has stepped up in the next iteration of the show

Audiences have only been given a glimpse of what to expect from the second series of All's Fair so far.

Co-star Watts, who also serves as a producer on the show alongside Kardashian, says they have "doubled down" on "the high fashion, high drama and heightened reality" that audiences enjoyed the first time around.

As for Kardashian's acting, Watts says she's on a "trajectory" that sees her "stepping up in the second season".

"She was improvising, riffing, doing all kind of things that I thought were deeply impressive," Watts adds, to which Kardashian jokes: "I think I'm just naturally so funny."

One of the positives that critics did cite was the show's desire to spotlight the duality of professional women who were both feminine and successful, which Kardashian says she "loves" because it is "a really realistic depiction of a lot of women I know".

"It doesn't mean that just because you're super smart that you can't be fashionable and into glamorous things as well," she adds.

title: ‘Hardest days of my life,’ goalkeeper Owono mourns late striker
excerpt: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono said on Wednesday that he is enduring the “hardest days of my life” after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, whom he collided with ...
description: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono said on Wednesday that he is enduring the “hardest days of my life” after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, whom he collided with ...
content:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono said on Wednesday that he is enduring the “hardest days of my life” after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, whom he collided with during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

The 30-year-old Spanish footballer died on Tuesday as a result of injuries he suffered in the sickening collision with Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who had raced into midfield to clear an aerial ball.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

“These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra.

“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him.

“I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus,” he added.

Spanish police sources told AFP an investigation into what happened has been opened, under judicial supervision.

Andorra players observed a minute’s silence on Wednesday before a voluntary training session, which Owono, 25, did not attend.

Owono received support from the president of the African country’s federation, Venancio Tomas Micha, in a letter of condolence following De Miguel’s death.

“I feel compelled to convey all our solidarity and support at this time to our player Jesus Lazaro Owono,” Tomas Micha wrote.

“We know that, as the involuntary protagonist of this tragic incident in the game, he is living through this situation with deep sorrow and distress.

“From the Equatorial Guinea Football Federation, we offer him all our human and professional backing, fully aware of the harshness of this event, which no one in our sport ever wishes to witness.”

Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz posted on Instagram in support of Owono, whom he said was “deeply affected” by what had happened.

“Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone,” wrote Spatz.

“In football, unfortunate incidents can happen but no one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences.”

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Earlier it was confirmed Tenerife and Andorra’s Spanish second division matches scheduled for the weekend would be postponed.

Tenerife were due to face Granada away from home, while Andorra were set to welcome Mallorca.

“After the tragic news of the death of Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel, the game… this Saturday November 7, at Nuevo Los Carmenes (stadium), has been postponed,” said Granada in a statement.

Mallorca said “at times like this, respect and sensitivity in the face of a situation of profound grief must come first”.

The Spanish football federation postponed all Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches this week as a mark of respect following De Miguel’s death.

Tenerife plan to hold a tribute to De Miguel at the club’s stadium on Saturday which supporters can attend, and are holding a six-day mourning period.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The club said the first team, board and staff will attend De Miguel’s funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa, in the province of Toledo on the Spanish mainland, where he has family roots.

A minute of silence was held before Champions League matches on Tuesday in honour of the striker, with the same planned for the rest of the week’s fixtures organised by European football governing body UEFA.

title: Atiku urges Senate to reject Tinubu’s $7.7bn loan request
excerpt: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has urged the Senate to reject President Bola Tinubu’s latest $7.7bn external borrowing request, warning that the proposed loan would furthe...
description: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has urged the Senate to reject President Bola Tinubu’s latest $7.7bn external borrowing request, warning that the proposed loan would furthe...
content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has urged the Senate to reject President Bola Tinubu’s latest $7.7bn external borrowing request, warning that the proposed loan would further burden Nigerians and future administrations.

Atiku, in a statement issued on Wednesday by the Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, described the frequency of the Federal Government’s borrowing requests as alarming.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The proposed $7.7bn loan, estimated at ₦10.79tn, is expected to part-finance the 2026 budget deficit.

The opposition politician’s reaction came barely days after another external borrowing proposal of $20.52bn and €1.045bn was presented to the National Assembly for approval.

Questioning the government’s borrowing strategy, Atiku said Nigerians should not be expected to treat the successive requests as routine legislative business.

“What is the problem with this government? Why is President Tinubu making borrowing requests on behalf of Nigeria week in, week out?

“Every new foreign loan is a bill Nigerians will eventually have to pay. This government cannot keep presenting borrowing as a substitute for sound economic management while families and businesses carry the cost of its failures,” he said.

The ADC presidential candidate called on the Senate to subject the latest proposal to rigorous scrutiny, insisting that the government must provide details of the projects to be financed, their respective costs, the interest rates, repayment schedules and other conditions attached to the facility.

He also questioned the provision in the President’s letter indicating that the final borrowing terms would depend on prevailing market conditions when the loan was priced.

“Nigerians should not be asked to accept a loan before they know what it will cost the country,” he added.

The ADC chieftain urged lawmakers to demand a comprehensive project list, clear funding allocations and a credible repayment plan before considering the request.

“No government should receive a blank cheque to contract foreign debt in the name of budget implementation,” he added.

Atiku further called on international lenders and agencies to suspend fresh lending to the Tinubu administration until it provides transparent loan terms, a credible repayment plan and evidence of the benefits of previous borrowings.

He accused the President of presiding over a worsening cost-of-living crisis despite the removal of petrol subsidy and the government’s continued access to foreign loans.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“Tinubu removed subsidy on petroleum products but has emerged as the highest borrowing government in Nigeria’s record history,” he noted.

Atiku also faulted the administration over what he described as inadequate infrastructure investment and the absence of effective social welfare interventions, arguing that Nigerians were struggling to afford basic necessities while the country’s debt continued to rise.

He, however, said his proposed alternative would include the restoration of social welfare programmes through what he described as a production-based subsidy on petroleum products.

The former vice president maintained that Nigeria could not continue to borrow its way out of every budget deficit, urging the National Assembly to prioritise the interests of citizens in its consideration of the loan request.

“The National Assembly must remember that it is accountable to Nigerians, not merely to the executive.

“Before approving another trillion-naira burden, it must make the government answer the questions Nigerians are asking,” he stressed.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The latest controversy comes amid sustained debate over Nigeria’s rising public debt, the cost of servicing existing obligations and the government’s reliance on borrowing to finance infrastructure and budgetary commitments.

While the Federal Government has repeatedly defended borrowing as necessary to fund development and bridge revenue gaps, opposition figures have called for greater transparency and accountability in the management of public debt.

title: 2027: Atiku vows to restore fuel subsidy, reopen borders
excerpt: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to restore fuel subsidy, reopen Nigeria’s land borders for legitimate trade and tackle...
description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to restore fuel subsidy, reopen Nigeria’s land borders for legitimate trade and tackle...
content:
The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to restore fuel subsidy, reopen Nigeria’s land borders for legitimate trade and tackle insecurity if elected president in 2027.

Atiku made the pledge on Wednesday during the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto, which attracted thousands of supporters.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He said his administration would focus on improving security, reviving the economy and promoting cross-border trade, particularly in Northern Nigeria, where many communities depend on commercial activities with neighbouring countries.

“I will open all the land borders for our people to do legitimate business with our brothers across the border.

“We will restore subsidy back into our fuel and do everything humanly possible to bring an end to insecurity so as to ensure our people can go back to our farms,” he said.

The former Vice-President urged Nigerians to participate in the 2027 elections, vote for the ADC and protect their votes to ensure they are properly counted.

He said the party would resist any attempt to manipulate the electoral process.

“We should all come out, vote massively, protect our votes and make sure our votes are counted and announced. We will not allow what happened in the last elections to happen anymore,” Atiku said.

He also described Sokoto as an important political and historical centre in Northern Nigeria and West Africa, citing its position as the seat of the Sokoto Caliphate.

Atiku thanked the state party leadership for organising the campaign flag-off, alleging that the ruling party in Sokoto had opposed the rally.

Earlier, the ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, said the turnout at the event showed that residents of Sokoto were ready for political change.

Mark noted that the delegation spent more than three hours travelling from the airport to the rally venue, a distance of less than 10 kilometres, attributing the delay to the large crowd of supporters.

He described the combination of Atiku and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, as the leadership needed to address the country’s security and economic challenges.

Mark also said the ADC would work to reverse what he described as its failures.

In his remarks, Amaechi said the 2027 election should be determined by the economic conditions of Nigerians rather than religious or ethnic considerations.

He urged voters to assess the Tinubu administration based on the cost of living and its performance in office, adding that the country needed leadership capable of addressing the hardship facing citizens.

Also speaking, former Sokoto State Governor and Senator representing Sokoto South, Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, urged Nigerians to vote out the ruling All Progressives Congress in 2027.

Tambuwal accused the Tinubu administration of failing to address insecurity, poverty, hunger and infrastructure challenges.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He said the election should be about providing effective leadership rather than supporting candidates based on political alliances or regional considerations.

“It is not about supporting our own leaders. It is about delivering leadership to this country,” he said.

He called on supporters to mobilise for the ADC ahead of the elections.

At the event, Mark also presented the ADC flag to the party’s Sokoto State governorship candidate, Muhammad Manir Dan’Iya.

The Atiku-led delegation arrived at the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport shortly after 1pm but reached the rally venue shortly before 5pm.

Thousands of supporters from different parts of the state gathered at the airport and along adjoining roads to welcome the presidential candidate and attend the campaign flag-off.

Atiku’s promises come amid an ongoing debate over the economic policies of the President Bola Tinubu administration, particularly the removal of the petrol subsidy in May 2023.

The former Vice-President has repeatedly pledged to restore the subsidy if elected in 2027, while proposing a targeted intervention for locally refined petroleum products.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The APC Presidential Campaign Council has, however, challenged him to explain how the proposal would be funded and implemented.

On the proposed reopening of land borders, the Federal Government had disputed Atiku’s claim that Nigeria’s borders remained closed, saying several major land borders had been reopened for trade under previous and current administrations.

content:
Troops of the Joint Task Force North-West, Operation Fansan Yamma, have rescued nine kidnapped victims and recovered 108 livestock during separate operations in Danko-Wasagu Local Government Area of Kebbi State.

The operations, conducted by troops of Sector 2 around Danko, Sabon Tunga and Binoni communities, also led to the recovery of 34 cows and 74 rams.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The military disclosed this in a statement, saying the troops responded to a distress call over the invasion of communities in the Danko general area by suspected bandits, who reportedly kidnapped residents and rustled cattle.

According to the statement, the troops immediately mobilised to the affected area and engaged the suspected bandits in a gun battle, forcing them to flee and abandon their captives.

title: Nigeria can become Africa’s rice export hub — NGF
excerpt: …Forum says 5.3m-tonne production deficit can be bridged, urges states to establish data banks
description: …Forum says 5.3m-tonne production deficit can be bridged, urges states to establish data banks
content:
…Forum says 5.3m-tonne production deficit can be bridged, urges states to establish data banks

ABUJA — The Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) has expressed optimism that Nigeria can become a major rice exporter in Africa, insisting that the country’s agricultural potential and available human, financial and natural resources are sufficient to achieve the ambition.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The forum said Nigeria could close its 5.3 million metric tonnes rice production deficit and become a net exporter if governments addressed policy inconsistencies, improved agricultural data and provided sustained support to farmers and other players across the value chain.

The Director-General of the NGF, Dr. Abdulateef Shittu, stated this on Wednesday in Abuja during the launch of the Northwest Rice Diagnostic Report organised by the forum.

Shittu said Nigeria currently consumed about 8.6 million metric tonnes of rice annually, a figure projected to rise to 9.1 million metric tonnes next year, while domestic production stood at only 3.3 million metric tonnes.

He blamed the production shortfall on inconsistent government policies, poor coordination and other challenges affecting the agricultural sector.

According to him, Nigeria has no justification for remaining dependent on imported rice, given its agricultural resources and capacity to supply regional African markets and parts of Europe.

He cited China’s transition from food deficit to self-sufficiency through targeted investments, saying Nigeria needed similar political commitment to achieve food security.

Shittu said: “You can see the huge gap. So, how do we address this? There are a lot of policy flip-flops, policy mismatch, and quite a number of other challenges that we will all have to address. But my motto simply is that there is no problem without a solution.

“We have all the resources, both human and material. We have the land and everything that we need to support farmers and other actors across the value chain. Whatever they need can be guaranteed.”

He described credible data as central to agricultural planning and disclosed that the NGF had established a dedicated data department to improve the collection and management of information across states.

He urged all 36 states to establish functional Bureaus of Statistics, noting that Kaduna and some other states had already taken the initiative.

According to him, national statistics, including Gross Domestic Product figures, should reflect aggregated data from the states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The NGF boss said the forum was also challenging figures presented by development partners where it believed they were inaccurate.

“If we are saying it is not correct, we have to show them which one is correct,” he said.

He added that heads of State Bureaus of Statistics met quarterly under a committee of practice, while commissioners of agriculture also held periodic meetings to exchange ideas and experiences.

Shittu disclosed that the forum had signed a partnership with the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA), Ibadan, and established the NGF Academy and Leadership Centre to strengthen governance capacity across key sectors.

He described the Northwest Rice Diagnostic Report as “not a destination, but a journey”, saying it would be the first in a series of engagements aimed at addressing challenges in the agricultural sector.

He acknowledged the difficult position of governments, which had to balance consumers’ concerns over rising rice prices with the need to protect farmers and millers.

Meanwhile, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Bank of Agriculture (BOA), Ayodeji Oludare Sotinrin, disclosed that the bank financed 25 aggregators during the preceding wet season, facilitating input credit for more than 500,000 farmers.

He said the bank planned to expand the facility to at least 700,000 farmers in the current farming cycle.

Sotinrin explained that the bank had shifted from direct cash disbursements to structured input financing because of challenges with loan recovery.

He said the arrangement ensured that farmers received essential agricultural inputs rather than cash that could be diverted to other purposes.

The BOA chief also disclosed plans to introduce guaranteed minimum prices for rice and other staple crops to protect farmers against market volatility.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He said the bank was developing financing arrangements around 15 dams in Kano State and other irrigation networks to support all-year-round rice production.

On mechanisation, Sotinrin said the bank was adding 2,000 tractors and 14,000 implements to its existing fleet, following an earlier rollout of 2,000 tractors and 10,000 implements.

He said the equipment would be deployed through specialised mechanisation service providers rather than distributed directly to individual farmers.

According to him, the 4,000 tractors, operating at an estimated capacity of 600 hectares annually per tractor, could support the cultivation of about 2.4 million hectares yearly.

On state partnerships, he disclosed that the bank was establishing sub-funds with matching contributions from state governments, including a N10 billion facility with Kaduna State, whose funds had already been paid into the bank’s account.

Speaking on behalf of the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA), Mr. Phillip Obosi said a stable and predictable policy environment was necessary to sustain an internationally competitive rice sector.

He warned that regulatory inconsistencies could discourage private investment, noting that Nigeria’s projected rice imports of 2.9 million metric tonnes in 2026, valued at approximately $1.4 billion, represented a significant drain on foreign exchange reserves.

Obosi, who cited United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) projections, urged governments to translate the report’s recommendations into budgetary allocations and practical programmes targeting input dealers, smallholder farmers and mechanisation providers.

Earlier, the Director-General of the Rice Processors Association of Nigeria (RIPAN), Dr. Andy Ekwelem, identified poor farmer identification, unreliable baseline data, adulterated agricultural inputs, weak extension services and insecurity in rural communities as major challenges confronting commercial rice production and processing.

He urged federal and state governments to establish verified farmer registers, provide certified seeds and fertilisers, conduct soil testing and secure major agricultural corridors, particularly in Kaduna, Katsina, Zamfara and Sokoto states.

Ekwelem also called for measures to reduce rising energy costs and operational expenses for local millers, warning that domestic processors were struggling to compete with foreign imports supported by decades of government subsidies.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

In separate remarks, the Commissioners for Agriculture in Kaduna and Kebbi states, Murtala Dabo and Shehu Muazu, called for reliable data systems, price stability and structured market protection for farmers.

Dabo advocated guaranteed prices and strategic grain reserves to stabilise farmers’ incomes, while Muazu called for harmonised data collection procedures between federal and state agencies to eliminate conflicting agricultural production statistics.

title: 2027: We won’t endorse any candidate — Health workers
excerpt: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 elections, the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN) on Wednesday declared that its members will not endorse or finance any candidate.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The health workers also said they are rejecting a spectator role in the forthcoming elections and demanded binding commitments on CONHESS and outstanding arrears.

Speaking in his welcome address at the 52nd session of the National Executive Council (NEC) meeting in Abuja, the President of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria, Comrade Kabiru Ado Sani, said the union will enter the 2027 general election neither as party loyalists nor as passive observers, but as an organised constituency demanding enforceable commitments on welfare, CONHESS arrears, and outstanding collective agreements.

In a strongly worded position ahead of the polls, the union said the question confronting health workers is no longer whether they will participate in the election, but on what terms.

“The permutation is now upon us. The question is no longer whether health workers will be in it, but whether we shall be in it as spectators, as foot soldiers, or as a constituency with a strong position,” the MHWUN President said.

He warned that health workers must not allow their numerical strength and professional importance to be reduced to election-season mobilisation for politicians who may abandon their concerns afterwards.

MHWUN insisted that it remains a trade union, not a political party, and would not endorse any candidate or political platform.

“MHWUN is a trade union, not a political party. We will not endorse any party or candidate, and the funds of this Union will not be used to finance any of them,” the union leader stated.

He added that members remain free to vote according to their conscience, stressing that no individual has the authority to speak for the union while campaigning for a party.

“Our members are free to vote their conscience, and no one speaks for this Union when speaking for a party,” he said.

The union argued that its political influence should not depend on telling members whom to vote for, but on forcing every contender for power to confront the health sector’s unresolved demands.

“Our influence does not lie in telling members how to vote. It lies in making the health worker’s agenda impossible to ignore, whoever wins,” the MHWUN political head declared.

He explained that at the centre of that agenda are the CONHESS salary structure, unpaid arrears, and collective agreements reached with the Federal Government but yet to be fully implemented.

The union framed its demands in legal as well as moral terms, insisting that agreements signed by the Federal Government cannot be treated as disposable political promises.

“A collective agreement signed by the Federal Government is an obligation of the State,” Dr. Sani said. “It does not lapse when a tenure ends, and no incoming administration is entitled to treat it as the debt of its predecessor.”

He warned that any administration emerging from the 2027 polls would inherit not only government assets and the treasury, but also outstanding obligations to health workers.

“Whoever is declared winner after 16th January will inherit the CONHESS table, the arrears, and the unconcluded negotiations, along with the Treasury,” he said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

While pressing for a strong health-worker voice, MHWUN urged members to participate lawfully and peacefully in the electoral process, avoiding conduct capable of damaging the union’s reputation or exposing members to risk.

“I therefore urge every member to take part peacefully in the electoral process and not to take any action that would smear the good name of the union or jeopardise the interest of our members,” the union leader said.

He described the session as taking place at “a defining moment in our nation’s history,” citing a challenging economy and a general election just weeks away.“Comrades, specifically, in less than eleven weeks, Nigerians will go to the polls. Between now and then, every candidate of every party will discover and acknowledge health workers.”

He warned that health workers would be courted with familiar political language.“We will be called heroes, pillars of the nation, and the conscience of the health system. We shall hear it all with courtesy sugar-coated in a political tongue. But let us remember that warm words cost nothing, and that they have never paid a salary, cleared an arrear, or built infrastructure.”

The 52nd NEC meeting is holding under the theme, “Health Workers and Socio-Economic Crisis: Implications for the 2027 General Election.”

According to the MHWUN President, the theme is “not an invitation to join the political contest as a worker,” but “a clarion call to health workers to understand the implications of the outcome of the 2027 general election and how it affects the social and economic conditions of the Nigerian health worker.”

He said the Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU) has remained a potent instrument in the struggle for better welfare for health workers and improved funding of the health sector.

“CONHESS adjustment is one demand that is central to JOHESU’s struggle in the last thirteen years. This demand has led to many strike actions, the last being the historic 84-day strike action, which was suspended on 5th February 2026 on the strength of a signed Terms of Settlement (ToS) with the Federal Government.

“Regrettably, the Federal Government seems not to have learnt any lesson from the last strike action, as it has continued to drag and delay the matter against the spirit of the Terms of Settlement.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“The April 2026 date that was promised for implementation has passed without the CONHESS.

“Meanwhile, we are waiting for further directives from the two Labour Centres, the NLC and TUC, who promised to take over the demands,” he concluded.

…Says project launch most memorable day of her presidency

…Unveils 600-million-litre tank farm, 1,700km regional pipelineBy Udeme Akpan

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

President of Namibia, Dr Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, has described the $2.5 billion Dangote Namibia Tank Farm and Regional Pipeline Project as a landmark investment that will accelerate Africa’s industrialisation, enhance regional energy security and deepen economic integration across Southern Africa.

Speaking at the project’s official launch in Walvis Bay, the Namibian leader praised Aliko Dangote, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, for demonstrating confidence in Africa’s economic potential through transformative investments in energy infrastructure. She described the occasion as the most memorable day of her presidency.

“Today, is the most memorable day of my presidency,” she said, noting that the investment reflects the growing capacity of African entrepreneurs to drive the continent’s transformation.

The project comprises a proposed 600-million-litre petroleum storage facility and an approximately 1,700-kilometre regional pipeline network that will position Namibia as a strategic fuel distribution hub for Southern Africa.

The infrastructure is expected to improve fuel supply reliability, reduce transportation costs and support economic growth across the region.

President Nandi-Ndaitwah said the investment aligns with Namibia’s development priorities and the goals of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), while creating opportunities for employment, skills transfer and industrial expansion.Addressing the ceremony, Aliko Dangote said the investment forms part of the Group’s broader vision to build interconnected centres of production, storage and distribution across Africa.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He disclosed that the facility, located near Walvis Bay, will have storage capacity for 360 million litres of diesel and 240 million litres of petrol.

The pipeline network will connect Namibia to key markets in Botswana, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Malawi and parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo. “We want to invest heavily so that landlocked countries can access petroleum products at cheaper prices,” Dangote said.

Dangote also announced that the Group has increased its Africa-wide investment ambition towards 2030 from $50 billion to $60 billion, signalling plans for further expansion across the continent.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“What we are launching today represents an investment of $2.5 billion, but Namibia deserves much more. We want to invest more and do more with your government,” he said.

Reaffirming his commitment to Africa’s development, Dangote said the continent possesses the resources, talent and markets needed to achieve sustainable industrialisation. “Africa must industrialise Africa,” he declared.The Governor of Namibia’s Erongo Region, Dr Nathalia ǀGoagoses, also welcomed the investment, describing it as a strategic initiative that will strengthen Namibia’s role as a gateway for trade, investment and regional economic integration.Dangote concluded by reaffirming the Group’s long-term commitment to Namibia and Southern Africa, pledging continued investment in infrastructure projects that promote growth, job creation and prosperity across the continent.

…warns against burdening future govts

By Luminous Jannamike

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu over his request for another $7.7 billion foreign loan, warning against committing Nigerians and future administrations to mounting debt without full disclosure of how the money will be spent.

Atiku said the latest request, equivalent to about N10.79 trillion, was coming barely days after the Federal Government presented separate borrowing proposals of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to the National Assembly, raising questions about the administration’s appetite for foreign loans amid worsening economic hardship.

In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council, on Wednesday, Atiku questioned the frequency of the borrowing requests and demanded that the Senate subject the latest proposal to rigorous scrutiny.

“What is the problem with this government? Why is President Tinubu making borrowing requests on behalf of Nigeria week in, week out?” he queried.

He argued that Nigerians were being saddled with fresh debt obligations without sufficient explanation of the benefits of previous borrowings, while households and businesses continued to grapple with rising costs.

“Every new foreign loan is a bill Nigerians will eventually have to pay. This government cannot keep presenting borrowing as a substitute for sound economic management while families and businesses carry the cost of its failures,” he said.

Atiku specifically demanded disclosure of the projects to be funded, their individual costs, interest rates, repayment schedules and other conditions, noting that the President’s letter indicated that final loan terms would depend on market conditions when the borrowing was priced.

“No government should receive a blank cheque to contract foreign debt in the name of budget implementation,” he warned.

He also cautioned that Tinubu’s administration must not saddle Nigerians and succeeding governments with fresh financial obligations without demonstrating how previous loans had benefited the country.

Atiku called on international agencies and lenders to suspend fresh lending to the administration until it provides transparent borrowing terms, a credible repayment plan and clear evidence of the impact of previous loans.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Turning to the administration’s economic record, the former Vice President questioned why the removal of petroleum subsidy had not translated into improved living conditions, despite the scale of government borrowing.

“Tinubu removed subsidy on petroleum products but has emerged as the highest borrowing government in Nigeria’s record history,” he said.

He further accused the administration of presiding over worsening living conditions, inadequate infrastructure and the absence of effective social welfare interventions.

“Nigerians are hungry and angry. Public infrastructure are limited; social welfare intervention is non-existent. Yet Nigeria is owing massively under Tinubu,” he said.

Questioning the purpose of the fresh borrowing, Atiku asked: “What is Tinubu using his loans to finance specifically?”



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He said his alternative economic approach would include a production-based subsidy on petroleum products, which he described as a way of restoring social welfare and supporting productive economic activities.

Atiku urged the Senate to remember its accountability to Nigerians, insisting that lawmakers must obtain satisfactory answers on the proposed borrowing before approving another multitrillion-naira debt obligation.

content:
Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has sworn in three commissioners and 10 special advisers, urging them to remain humble, disciplined and committed to serving the people.

The governor warned the appointees against arrogance, indiscipline, corruption and abuse of public office, stressing that none of them should consider themselves indispensable.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Oyebanji gave the warning on Wednesday during the swearing-in ceremony at the Government House in Ado Ekiti.

He said his second term in office should not be an opportunity for complacency but a period to build on the achievements of his first administration and accelerate development in the state.

“I will like to counsel you to resist the temptation of the illusion of invincibility and indispensability, which could ultimately breed arrogance. At the end of the day, only God is truly indispensable.

“We must all therefore remain gracious and wholeheartedly dedicated to our unwavering service to the good people of Ekiti State,” he said.

The governor added that his administration would not condone unethical behaviour, unnecessary bureaucratic delays or avoidable mistakes capable of frustrating its development plans.

He urged the appointees to take their responsibilities seriously, noting that discipline and prompt service delivery would be central to his second term.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Oyebanji said his administration had put structures in place to ensure that the second term began without delays, adding that there was no time to waste in fulfilling its promises to the people.

The three commissioners sworn in are Mr Dayo Apata (SAN), Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice; Mr Akintunde Oyebode, Commissioner for Finance; and Dr Oyebanji Filani, Commissioner for Health and Human Services.

The 10 special advisers are Prof. James Olaleye, e-GIS, Lands and Survey; Mr James Folorunso, Bureau of Public Procurement; Dr John Moyo Ekundayo, Office of Transformation, Strategy and Delivery; Mr Bunmi Talabi, Bureau of Special Projects; and Mr Olayinka Oyebode, Media.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Others are Princess Adetoun Agboola, Special Education and Social Inclusion; Dr Gbenga Oyewole, Development, Planning and Budget; Mr Kayode Adaramodu, Economic Affairs and Private Sector Development; Mr Ebenezer Boluwade, Agriculture and Food Security; and Prof. Akeem Azeez, Special Duties.

Oyebanji was sworn in for a second term on October 16, following his re-election in the June 20 governorship election.

title: Sequoia hits rewind, undoing 20 years of expansion
excerpt: Sequoia Capital posted a memo to X on Wednesday morning titled “The Sequoia of Tomorrow” that’s full of surprises. The firm has raised roughly $10 billion in new funds, it says....
description: Sequoia Capital posted a memo to X on Wednesday morning titled “The Sequoia of Tomorrow” that’s full of surprises. The firm has raised roughly $10 billion in new funds, it says....
content:
Sequoia Capital posted a memo to X on Wednesday morning titled “The Sequoia of Tomorrow” that’s full of surprises. The firm has raised roughly $10 billion in new funds, it says. It is also closing its London office, shutting down its Arc accelerator and its Scouts program, merging its early-stage and growth teams into one, flattening its partnership, and killing the Monday partner meeting.

The framing is forward-looking, but the messaging is very much about rewinding to an earlier time when the team was smaller and focused more narrowly on Silicon Valley.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Sequoia says as much itself. The firm describes coming out of a roughly 20-year expansionary phase during which it built multiple businesses in multiple geographies and says an unintended side effect was hierarchy. Nearly everything being undone here was built during that stretch, under a succession of stewards running from Doug Leone through Jim Goetz to Roelof Botha.

One of the most surprising developments here is that the firm is killing two programs that put Sequoia closest to young founders. Scouts, which Sequoia launched around 2009 and, anecdotally, half the industry has since copied in some form, gave small checks to founders and operators to invest on the firm’s behalf; it was a way to see deals through people closer to interesting new founders than any partner could be. Jason Calacanis famously pointed Sequoia to Uber through the program. Sam Altman brought Stripe to Sequoia as a scout, too. Other early scouts included Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky and Dropbox founders Arash Ferdowsi and Drew Houston.

Arc, launched in March 2022, was Sequoia’s answer to Y Combinator: a batch accelerator for pre-seed and seed founders, running several cohorts a year for seven weeks, with admitted companies getting $500,000 to $1 million up front.

Both were bets on being early and being everywhere. Both are now gone, as Sequoia says it wants to put more energy behind fewer people and things.

So is London, which Sequoia opened in 2020 and is closing six years later. Several people will leave the firm. “We simply don’t see the need for a local presence,” the memo says, adding that Europe will keep producing outlier founders and that Sequoia can support them from the Bay Area. (If founders didn’t already feel pressured to move to the Bay Area or open an office in the region, they will now.)

Luciana Lixandru, hired from Accel in 2020 as Sequoia’s first partner in Europe, says she was offered a move to San Francisco and declined. (“Europe is where my family is, and where I want to build,” she wrote on X.) She says she remains a partner and will keep her board seats while investing personally in European founders.

For European founders, the message is going to be particularly difficult to digest, especially as it follows Andreessen Horowitz closing its London office last year and Coatue retreating in 2024. Sequoia didn’t say it won’t fund Europeans, but it’s definitely reinforcing here that the center of gravity is once again in the Bay Area.

The rewind extends to people too. The memo notes that Carl Eschenbach, the former Workday CEO, is very much back in the fold (he returned as a full-time partner in March). It also says the team has “reinvigorated the GOAT,” Doug Leone.

Though the nomenclature at venture firms is all over the place — including Sequoia — the memo makes clear there are now seven general partners who primarily own and operate Sequoia: Alfred Lin and Pat Grady — who are the firm’s co-stewards — along with Andrew Reed, Shaun Maguire, Konstantine Buhler, Sonya Huang, and David Cahn, who joined the firm in 2023.

And there are other changes. Jess Lee, the firm’s first female partner and an early-stage investor who oversaw its Arc program, is no longer shown on Sequoia’s investor page but rather as an operator; she remains with the firm as its chief product officer. Stephanie Zahn, an investor who had joined Sequoia in 2015, has meanwhile left the firm entirely, announcing last month that she is launching her own new firm.

Sequoia rarely lets anyone go entirely. Founder Don Valentine kept turning up at partner meetings for roughly a decade after handing over the firm. Goetz, who stepped back from his management responsibilities in 2017, is still featured on the firm’s site. Botha is the exception. He was voted out as senior steward last fall in a surprise shake-up — the firm framed it as a handoff to Lin and Grady — and he cut his remaining ties with Sequoia this summer, around the time he joined SpaceX’s board.

The changes are sure to make waves. Still, none of them are completely out of character. Sequoia iterates routinely, and sometimes that has meant retreating. Most notably, in 2023, it separated from its China and India/Southeast Asia arms, which became HongShan and Peak XV, ending a two-decade run as a global franchise under one name.

The rest of the memo is structural. It says the team has decided to dispense with its “early” and “growth” team approaches and operate as one. It also notes the Monday partner meeting — a ritual at Sequoia and at nearly every firm — is finished on the theory that founders operate around the clock and their investors should, too. (These may be going away more generally. At least, in a sit-down with TechCrunch at Disrupt last month, the entire Benchmark team suggested it now mostly uses Monday meetings to socialize.)

Sequoia acknowledges the moves come at some cost. “It is scary to break something that’s already working just fine,” the memo says, and painful to say goodbye to good people. Still, it’ll be a while before anyone knows if these were the right calls.

Here is Sequoia’s post in full:

We live in a world of accelerating change. The best founders reinvent themselves over and over again. We must do the same.

It’s been a year since our generational transition. We’ve been busy! We’re no longer evolving the Sequoia of yesterday; we are now building the Sequoia of tomorrow.

Here are a few of the changes we’ve made, and what they mean for founders.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Focus We are best at high-conviction, highly selective venture capital investing. This is our focus. We have removed much of the complexity associated with the Sequoia Capital Fund, sunset our batch accelerator (Arc) and Scouts programs, and streamlined both operating and investing teams. Putting more energy behind fewer people and things means better support for the founders we back.

One Team There is no more “Early & Growth”. There is only Sequoia. We are one team, operating under one shared mission. This should make things more seamless for founders as they go from stage to stage.

London We are closing our London office, which means several people will be leaving Sequoia. This is not about the team – they are excellent. We simply don’t see the need for a local presence. We believe that Europe will continue to produce outlier founders and companies, and that we can continue to provide world class support from our home base in the Bay Area.

Partners We are coming out of a ~20 year expansionary phase, during which we built multiple businesses in multiple geos. One unintended side effect was hierarchy; it required real management to run the operating side of our business, and this crept over into the investing team. We’ve made several internal changes that have the effect of flattening the partnership. This allows every partner to flourish, and every founder to receive the full benefit of Team Sequoia – regardless of who your lead partner happens to be.

Firepower We’ve welcomed two rising stars (Liam and Sonali) and one transcendentally talented founder & operator (Dev). We’ve reunited with a legendary leader (Carl) and reinvigorated the GOAT (Doug). We’ve elevated and empowered killer operators: Hem, Natalie, Rishi, Stacey, and Theresa. We’ve raised ~$10Bn in new funds. Talent and capital are two of the key ingredients in building legendary companies. Our talent density and capital base are stronger than ever.

24/7 There is no more Monday partner meeting cycle. Founders operate 24/7, and so do we. Founders shouldn’t have to adhere to our process – we will do our best to adhere to yours.

Some of these changes were obvious. Others less so. Many were hard. It is scary to break something that’s already working just fine, and it is painful to say goodbye to great people. We ask founders to do the right thing even when it is hard, and we are committed to doing the same.

Some things remain unchanged. Our mission is to help the daring build legendary companies, from idea to IPO and beyond. Our objective function is not scale, but quality: delivering the best possible returns to LPs, and being the best possible partner to founders.

Excellence is a moving target, so we will always be changing. But for now,



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

We have seven General Partners who own and operate our organization, and we are on offense: building our business so that we can support you in building yours. We are true believers, and as we enter a golden age of multiple tectonic shifts in parallel (AI, space, biology, reindustrialization, and perhaps more), we are so fired up for what’s to come. Let’s build something legendary together!

– Alfred, Andrew, David, Konstantine, Pat, Shaun, and Sonya, on behalf of Team Sequoia

title: ₦70,000 Transport Allowance: Labour veterans wade into crisis between NLC, TUC
excerpt: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — Labour veterans from the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) have intervened in the face-off between the President of the NLC, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and the TUC President, Comrade Festus Osifo.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The two labour leaders have recently traded words over the recent approval of ₦70,000 by the Federal Government to cushion the effect of high transportation costs occasioned by the removal of fuel subsidy.

The rift between the two leaders degenerated into personal attacks on national television, a situation that has affected unity within the labour sector.

Worried by the development, labour veterans met to bring the situation under control.

Speaking on Wednesday in Abuja at the 52nd session of the National Executive Council (NEC) of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN), Comrade Wabba said the labour veterans had been able to arrest any form of hostility between the two leaders.

The former NLC President told journalists that veterans from the two labour centres had met to resolve what he described as a family misunderstanding between the two centres.

He said the veterans emphasised that workers’ organisations must remain united because they share a single objective and aim.

The former President of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC) said all hostilities had been ordered to stop, explaining that the goal is to prevent future occurrences through formal dialogue.

He said: “It’s a family misunderstanding between the two centres, and we have made it clear that workers’ organisations are supposed to be one because the objective is one and the aim is one.

“So, that seeming misunderstanding has escalated, and we have said all hostilities should stop. We will actually try to meet with them to see what happened and how future occurrences can also be prevented.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“So, basically, I can tell you for sure that veterans from both sides—TUC and NLC—namely Peter Esele, Bobboi Kaigama, Hassan Sunmonu, Abdulwaheed Omar, and my humble self, actually met and tried to look at the issue. We said we would meet formally when all of them are available because we just communicated among ourselves, the veterans, and we communicated with them, and they mutually accepted.

“The TUC General Secretary was here; I was here; the NLC President was here. All of us embraced ourselves and said,

‘Well, it’s a family issue.’ Therefore, we have also said members of the press should not actually try to advance issues that are not there because, even in your immediate family, you can have some internal issues.

“But that internal issue is certainly meant to be resolved, and we are working towards that very effectively because that is the hallmark of trade unionism: to resolve issues, even with our employers, through dialogue and social dialogue. So, basically, it is an issue we have practised, and therefore we will try to now put it into action.”

The former NLC President said some of the protagonists in the matter had travelled, adding that once they returned, “we will be able to have that platform to address the issue.”



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“But for the meantime, we said we don’t see the necessity of further talking to the press because that, in itself, does not bring any solution.”

Speaking earlier, the NLC President, Comrade Ajaero, said the agreed ₦70,000 transport intervention had become secured for workers and that, when discussions for a new minimum wage begin, the money would form part of what would be added.

title: Reps propose licence revocation for hospitals denying emergency care
excerpt: The House of Representatives has begun moves to strengthen enforcement of patients’ right to emergency medical care, proposing tougher sanctions, including suspension or withdra...
description: The House of Representatives has begun moves to strengthen enforcement of patients’ right to emergency medical care, proposing tougher sanctions, including suspension or withdra...
content:
The House of Representatives has begun moves to strengthen enforcement of patients’ right to emergency medical care, proposing tougher sanctions, including suspension or withdrawal of operating licences, for hospitals that refuse, delay or obstruct treatment.

This followed the second reading on Wednesday of a bill sponsored by the member representing Ikole/Oye Federal Constituency of Ekiti State, Mr Akin Rotimi which seeks to amend the National Health Act, 2014, by introducing mandatory emergency triage, stabilisation and referral procedures, with clearly defined timelines and enforceable obligations for healthcare facilities and professionals.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Under the proposed legislation, hospitals would be required to commence triage within 15 minutes of a patient’s arrival and basic stabilisation within 30 minutes, while life-saving interventions must begin immediately once a life-threatening condition is identified, irrespective of administrative procedures.

Leading the debate on the general principles of the bill, Rotimi said the proposed amendment was designed to address preventable deaths and complications arising from delays in accessing emergency medical care.

He lamented that despite existing legal provisions protecting patients’ right to emergency treatment, Nigerians continued to suffer avoidable consequences because of administrative bottlenecks, demands for payment before treatment, unavailable hospital beds and poorly coordinated referrals.

“Mr Speaker, in a medical emergency, time is the difference between life and death. Yet, Nigerians continue to lose their lives or suffer preventable complications because of delays arising from administrative bottlenecks, demands for payment before treatment, unavailable hospital beds and poorly coordinated referrals,” he said.

Rotimi noted that although Section 20 of the National Health Act, 2014, prohibits the refusal of emergency medical treatment, experience has demonstrated the need for clearer operational standards and stronger enforcement mechanisms.

“Although the National Health Act, 2014, prohibits the refusal of emergency medical treatment, experience demonstrates the need to reinforce this obligation with clear operational standards and enforceable accountability. The right to emergency treatment must translate into timely assessment, immediate life-saving intervention, stabilisation and effective referral where necessary,” he added.

The proposed amendment also seeks to address delays caused by shortages of medical personnel, allowing trained and certified nurses to conduct triage where a medical practitioner is unavailable.

On emergency admission and referral, healthcare facilities would be required to assign a bed to an emergency patient within two hours where one is available.

Where no bed is available, the facility must commence stabilisation and initiate referral within two hours of the patient’s arrival or immediately upon clinical stabilisation.

The bill further stipulates that transportation should be arranged within 30 minutes of a referral decision, while the transfer should be completed within three hours, except where circumstances beyond the facility’s control prevent compliance.

Beyond response timelines, the proposed legislation introduces stricter penalties for healthcare establishments and professionals that fail to discharge their emergency care responsibilities.

Hospitals that refuse, delay or obstruct emergency treatment could face financial penalties, suspension of their operating licences and, in cases of subsequent offences, possible closure or withdrawal of their licences.

Healthcare professionals who wilfully refuse or abandon emergency patients could also face criminal sanctions and professional disciplinary proceedings.

The proposal, however, recognises that healthcare facilities sometimes operate under genuine resource constraints. It provides protection for healthcare workers who act in good faith, properly document resource limitations and comply with established referral procedures.

It also proposes that patients or their representatives could seek compensation through civil action against healthcare facilities where injury, disability or death results from a contravention of the emergency treatment provisions.

Explaining the rationale behind the proposed legislation, Rotimi said the objective was to protect lives while restoring public confidence in the country’s healthcare system.

“Mr Speaker, Honourable Colleagues, this bill is fundamentally about protecting human life and strengthening public confidence in our healthcare system.

“An emergency patient depends on the readiness, competence and responsiveness of the healthcare facility. Every unnecessary delay increases the risk of deterioration, disability or death. Our laws must therefore establish clear responsibilities and minimum standards for timely intervention,” he stressed.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The lawmaker said the proposed amendment also acknowledged the challenges confronting healthcare delivery in Nigeria by distinguishing genuine resource limitations from negligence and wilful abandonment of patients.

He argued that mandatory training, professional certification and standardised emergency care procedures would improve preparedness among healthcare workers, strengthen referral coordination and establish clearer lines of responsibility when emergency treatment is delayed.

The bill mandates the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria to jointly develop and maintain a standardised national emergency care curriculum.

Healthcare workers involved in emergency care would be required to undergo mandatory training and certification at intervals not exceeding 18 months.

Rotimi maintained that the ability of healthcare institutions to respond effectively to emergencies was a critical measure of the strength of any health system.

“Mr Speaker, the true strength of a healthcare system is demonstrated not only by the quality of its routine services but also by its capacity to respond when lives are at immediate risk. Every Nigerian deserves timely and appropriate emergency medical attention, irrespective of circumstance or location,” he said.

Urging lawmakers to support the bill, he argued that no Nigerian should be compelled to negotiate for treatment at a time when immediate medical attention could determine whether a patient survives.

“No Nigerian should have to negotiate for survival at the point of a medical emergency. No family should lose a loved one because treatment was unnecessarily delayed, a referral was poorly coordinated or a healthcare facility failed to discharge its responsibility.

“This bill provides an important legislative step towards emergency medical care that is timely, competent, coordinated and accountable.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“It seeks to ensure that the right to emergency treatment is not merely declared in our laws but reflected in the actual delivery of healthcare. I therefore urge Honourable Members to support the general principles of this Bill and allow it to proceed to the Committee Stage in the interest of safeguarding the lives and wellbeing of Nigerians. I so move. Thank you,” he argued.

The proposed amendment comes amid longstanding concerns over access to emergency medical services in Nigeria, where patients and their families have faced difficulties securing urgent treatment because of financial barriers, inadequate facilities, shortages of medical personnel and poor referral arrangements.

title: Senate proposes jail, N300,00 fine for hospitals rejecting emergency patients
excerpt: The Senate is considering a bill seeking a six-month jail term or a fine of up to N300,000 for hospitals and healthcare providers that violate proposed emergency treatment stand...
description: The Senate is considering a bill seeking a six-month jail term or a fine of up to N300,000 for hospitals and healthcare providers that violate proposed emergency treatment stand...
content:
The Senate is considering a bill seeking a six-month jail term or a fine of up to N300,000 for hospitals and healthcare providers that violate proposed emergency treatment standards.

The bill also seeks to compel public and private hospitals to assess emergency patients within 15 minutes of arrival, commence initial stabilisation within 30 minutes and complete referrals to other facilities within three hours where necessary.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Sponsored by Senator Abdulaziz Yar’Adua, the proposed legislation seeks to amend the National Health Act, 2014, to establish enforceable standards for emergency medical treatment, healthcare workers’ training and patient referral procedures.

Leading the debate at Wednesday’s plenary, Yar’Adua said the amendment would address critical gaps in Nigeria’s healthcare system and ensure that patients received timely, life-saving treatment during emergencies, irrespective of their social status, wealth, influence or location.

He said, “The Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria shall jointly develop and maintain a standardised national emergency care curriculum, and all healthcare workers involved in the provision of emergency medical care shall be required to undergo such training and certification at intervals not exceeding 18 months.

“Public and private healthcare facilities licensed to provide emergency medical care in Nigeria shall commence triage and initial assessment within 15 minutes of a patient’s arrival at the emergency department. Where a licensed medical doctor is unavailable, a trained and certified nurse may conduct the triage.

“A person or health facility that contravenes any provision of this section commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding ₦300,000 or imprisonment for a term not exceeding six (6) months, or both.”

The proposed amendment further requires hospitals to begin basic stabilisation measures, including oxygen therapy, intravenous fluids, pain relief and preliminary diagnostic procedures, within 30 minutes of a patient’s arrival.

It also mandates immediate life-saving interventions, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation, airway management and bleeding control, once a life-threatening condition is identified.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Where a patient requires admission, the hospital would be required to assign a bed within two hours, subject to availability.

However, facilities without available beds must immediately stabilise patients and commence referral arrangements within two hours of arrival or as soon as the patient is assessed and considered stable for transfer.

The bill also requires hospitals to begin ambulance dispatch or arrange alternative transportation within 30 minutes of deciding to refer a patient.

Yar’Adua said the proposed amendment was consistent with international practices, citing Ghana, South Africa, Kenya, the United Kingdom and the United States.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Supporting the bill, the Senate Whip, Senator Mohammed Monguno (APC, Borno North), said it would address avoidable deaths arising from road accidents and maternal emergencies.

He lamented that some healthcare providers neglected emergency patients, resulting in preventable deaths, adding that the proposed legislation would introduce criminal liability for violations of emergency treatment standards.

title: Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar
excerpt: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR
description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR
content:
By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR

The Cross River State Police Command on Wednesday arrested a 27-year-old man, Victor Edet Yellow Duke, in connection with an attack on the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, in Calabar, the state capital.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The attack left the windshields of some vehicles smashed.

The incident occurred at about 2:20 p.m. at the Watt Market Roundabout as the convoy was returning from the palace of the Obong of Calabar to Metropolitan Hotel, the venue of the party’s presidential town hall meeting.

According to the police, a group of suspected hoodlums, reportedly armed with machetes and sticks, emerged from the Calabar Road and Clerks Alley axis and attacked vehicles in the convoy.

The number of vehicles affected had not been ascertained.

Police personnel deployed in the area moved in swiftly to contain the situation. Their intervention, which included the use of tear gas, led to the arrest of the suspect, while the other attackers fled.

The suspect was later taken to the State Police Headquarters by operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, VCRU, for what the command described as a discreet investigation, to prevent reprisals or a further breakdown of law and order. Normalcy has since returned to the area.

In a statement by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, the command said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, had ordered a thorough investigation to identify and arrest other participants and establish the full circumstances of the incident.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Cautioning against presuming the suspect’s guilt, the police said: “The arrest of a suspect does not amount to a determination of guilt, as the suspect remains entitled to the presumption of innocence pending the conclusion of investigation and any subsequent judicial proceedings.”

The command assured residents, political stakeholders and visitors that adequate security measures remained in place across the state.

It reiterated its commitment to “providing equal security protection to all political parties, candidates and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation.”



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

It also urged the public to stay calm, avoid spreading unverified information and report suspicious activities through established police channels.

Eitokpah added: “The Cross River State Police Command remains committed to maintaining public safety, protecting democratic participation and ensuring that all lawful political activities are conducted in a peaceful and secure environment.”
