title: NNPC posts N3.49trn profit in nine months
excerpt: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja
description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja
content:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

ABUJA — The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) recorded a cumulative Profit After Tax (PAT) of N3.494 trillion between January and September 2026, following an 18.1 per cent increase in its September profit to N509 billion.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The September profit rose from N431 billion recorded in August, according to the company’s September 2026 Monthly Operations and Financial Report.

The latest figures bring NNPC’s cumulative profit for the first nine months of 2026 to N3.494 trillion.

A breakdown of the performance showed that the company recorded profits of N385 billion in January, N136 billion in February, N276 billion in March, N481 billion in April, N462 billion in May, N535 billion in June, N279 billion in July, N431 billion in August and N509 billion in September.

The report also showed that NNPC generated N33.152 trillion in revenue during the nine-month period.

Its September revenue stood at N4.608 trillion, representing a 23.3 per cent increase from the N3.737 trillion recorded in August.

Monthly revenue figures showed that the company generated N2.571 trillion in January, N2.680 trillion in February, N2.774 trillion in March, N4.971 trillion in April, N4.335 trillion in May, N4.389 trillion in June and N3.087 trillion in July.

On its statutory obligations, NNPC disclosed that payments to the Federation Account and other statutory remittances rose to N11.14 trillion between January and September.

The amount represents an increase of 17.4 per cent, or N1.65 trillion, over the N9.49 trillion recorded between January and August.

On the operational front, average crude oil and condensate production stood at 1.70 million barrels per day in September.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Natural gas production also increased to 7,789 million standard cubic feet per day, compared with 7,680 million standard cubic feet per day recorded in August.

Total hydrocarbon production, comprising crude oil, condensate and natural gas equivalent, averaged 3.04 million barrels of oil equivalent per day during the period.

The company further reported 100 per cent availability of its upstream pipeline infrastructure in September.

On gas infrastructure projects, NNPC said the Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) Gas Pipeline had achieved 100 per cent completion, while the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) Gas Pipeline was 95 per cent complete.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

It added that the OB3 River Niger Crossing pipeline had been commissioned and operationalised.

According to the company, collaboration with relevant stakeholders was ongoing to accelerate construction and pre-commissioning activities on the AKK project, with a target of delivering early gas supply to Abuja before the end of 2026.

title: Atiku vows to restore fuel subsidy, reopen borders

By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO — Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to restore petroleum subsidy, tackle insecurity, reopen Nigeria’s land borders with neighbouring countries and reduce pilgrimage fares for Muslim and Christian faithful if elected president in 2027.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the pledges on Wednesday during the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto, where he outlined his proposed measures to address the country’s economic challenges, insecurity and declining standard of living.

He said his administration would prioritise the welfare of Nigerians, adding that restoring petroleum subsidy would be among the measures considered to ease the burden of rising fuel prices and reduce transportation costs and the prices of essential commodities.

The former vice-president also promised to take decisive steps to address insecurity across the country, protect lives and property and restore confidence in the nation’s security architecture.

He said Nigerians deserved to live and conduct their businesses without fear of attacks, kidnapping and other criminal activities.

On the economy, Atiku pledged to reopen Nigeria’s land borders with neighbouring countries to revive economic activities, strengthen regional trade and improve the livelihoods of communities dependent on cross-border commerce.

He said the move would create opportunities for traders, farmers and other economic operators while strengthening Nigeria’s commercial relations with neighbouring countries.

The ADC candidate also promised to reduce pilgrimage fares for Muslim and Christian faithful, arguing that the cost of religious journeys should not constitute an overwhelming burden for ordinary Nigerians.

He said his proposed administration would introduce policies to improve citizens’ welfare, expand economic opportunities and address the hardship confronting households.

Atiku urged Nigerians to support the ADC in the 2027 presidential election, saying the party would provide an alternative direction for the country.

Speaking at the rally, the ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, said the reception he witnessed from the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport to Sokoto metropolis indicated widespread support for the party in the state.

He expressed confidence that the people of Sokoto would vote for Atiku and other ADC candidates in the 2027 elections.

---

Also addressing the gathering, former Sokoto State Governor, Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led administration, accusing it of worsening poverty, hunger and insecurity across the country.

Tambuwal said the ruling party had failed to provide the leadership required to address Nigeria’s economic and security challenges.

He argued that Nigerians were facing severe economic difficulties, widespread hunger and persistent insecurity, insisting that the situation underscored the need for a change in leadership.

The former governor urged Nigerians to embrace the ADC as a political alternative, calling on them to support Atiku in the forthcoming election.

In his remarks, the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State assured Atiku of massive electoral support from the state, declaring that the party would mobilise its grassroots structures to secure votes for him in 2027.

“Your Excellency, Atiku Abubakar, Sokoto is your home, and we will prove that in 2027,” he said, amid cheers from party supporters.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The governorship candidate said the party would work to translate the enthusiasm surrounding Atiku’s candidacy into votes, urging members and supporters to remain united and committed to the ADC’s electoral campaign.

He described the campaign flag-off as an important step in the party’s preparations for the 2027 general elections.

title: I tried Apple’s Siri Recaps. They’re surprisingly useful — and a little unsettling
excerpt: On Tuesday, Apple rolled out a potentially controversial set of Audio Intelligence features into testing with the first developer beta versions of iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3. The...
description: On Tuesday, Apple rolled out a potentially controversial set of Audio Intelligence features into testing with the first developer beta versions of iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3. The...
content:
On Tuesday, Apple rolled out a potentially controversial set of Audio Intelligence features into testing with the first developer beta versions of iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3. The betas bring four new AI features that allow Apple Watch Series 12 wearers to detect important sounds, identify songs, catch up on conversations, and take notes.

After just a day with Apple’s Siri Recaps feature on my Apple Watch, I can already see how its value may ultimately outweigh any creepiness factor that comes from the AI-powered audio recording and summarization it provides. However, I also see areas where AI-assisted note-taking can go too far, capturing things that aren’t worth remembering, and where there’s room for improvement.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The first two, sound and song detection, don’t represent potential privacy concerns; they are designed to detect either important sounds — like an alarm or doorbell — or identify a song using Shazam’s technology. The former helps deaf and hard-of-hearing users navigate the world, and the latter is something we’ve already done with our iPhone for nearly two decades now.

It’s the two other features, Live Rewind and Siri Recaps, that have raised concerns. The features record and then transcribe or summarize the conversations happening with and around the Apple Watch’s owner. Live Rewind lets you go back to see what was said in the past 15 seconds, while Siri Recaps summarize audio throughout your day, saving notes of the important things that were said.

Apple has taken care to ensure the privacy of these AI features by processing the audio and running AI models on-device, when possible, and by not identifying speakers, storing raw audio files, and redacting private information, like government ID numbers or personal account information.

Still, some are put off by the idea that we’re now normalizing the idea that technology is always listening.

I find myself sympathizing with both camps. I often lament that we’ve allowed technology to become so pervasive in our daily lives, but I still see the value in what Apple has built.

I haven’t yet had an appropriate time to test Live Rewind, nor do I think this will be a feature I use as often. I’m more likely to say “sorry, what?” or “can you repeat that?” if I missed something that was said, before turning to my Apple Watch for help.

But with Siri Recaps, I immediately saw how this could become a feature I rely on regularly to save important notes for later.

I was able to test the feature in a real-world scenario yesterday, when we were dropping off my teen’s car for repairs and picking up a rental. At both places, employees shared a lot of information about time frames, prices, and policies that were delivered verbally. The information came too fast to stop and write anything down. Yet when I returned to Siri Recaps later in the day, it had captured key details that I may need to refer back to.

For instance, it noted the deductible, the repair time frame, the amount of gas we had in the rental at the start, and other things I wanted to remember.

One complaint is that Siri Recaps had mixed this information with other topics that were later discussed in the home, like an errand we needed to run and what time babysitting was this week, something we were discussing in order to create an appointment on the family calendar with an appropriate alert time frame.

I think these items should have been saved in a separate note titled “family schedule and errands,” rather than in the same note with the car repairs, but under a separate heading.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Because I configured Siri Recaps to run at all times, it also captured non-essential things, like our “plan” to watch the midterms coverage on TV, which is not the kind of thing you’d normally jot down a note about. It also was a stark reminder that the feature was listening in on our everyday conversations. That’s something that could feel invasive in different scenarios, if the subject being discussed was more personal in nature.

This had me considering turning off the Recap feature while at home in the evening, so family dinner table chatter doesn’t become note fodder.

While I appreciated that the Recap picked up a reminder about an errand I needed to run from one of the family conversations, other tidbits it saved — like what we were watching on TV — would only be valuable if you were exporting a Siri Recap note to Apple’s Journal app, because it was something you wanted to record for personal reasons.

I’d like to see these sorts of extraneous details saved as separate notes — or at least as dedicated sections that could be exported or deleted on their own at the end of the day.

I’d also love to be able to swipe left on an individual bullet point to remove it from the Siri Recap entirely, rather than having to enter edit mode, place the cursor, and then start deleting the text I don’t need.

Another option I’d like to have would be a setting that would allow you to automatically export any saved Siri Recap (the ones you click the bookmark icon to save) to Apple’s Notes app, instead of that being an extra step.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

These Recaps could go into their own folder in the Notes app for easy reference. I can understand why this option is not the default, given how many different ways people use a general-purpose app like Notes. However, it would be useful for those of us who want to keep Notes as the central starting point for all our jotted-down reminders and to-dos.

Though I wasn’t immediately warmed up to the idea that my Watch was always listening, so to speak, I see the value of this sort of automated note-taking in daily life.

content:
The Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, Brig. Gen. Buba Marwa (retd.), has solicited the support of traditional rulers in the fight against drug abuse in Nigeria.

Marwa spoke at the palace of the Oba of Benin, Ewuare II, on Tuesday while paying a courtesy visit during his visit to Benin City.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The NDLEA boss, who said he was in Edo State on an assessment visit to the agency’s state command and to address the Regimental Sergeant Majors Convention of the Nigerian Army, described drug abuse as one of the major scourges bedevilling the country.

“Over 15 million Nigerians are abusing drugs. This is three times the global average. It is a whole-of-society approach.

“We need the traditional institution, church, CSOs, government, media, because all hands must be on deck. But most importantly, the traditional institution,” he said.

While acknowledging the support the Oba of Benin had been giving in the fight against drug abuse, Marwa disclosed that the NDLEA had introduced a new pillar in drug control, which involves engaging communities involved in cannabis cultivation.

“Out of the 16 million kilograms of assorted illicit substances that we have seized in the last six years, 75 per cent is cannabis because we cultivate it in Nigeria. And Edo State is one of the cultivating states also.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“So, we have introduced alternative development as a strategic pillar in which we are appealing and persuading the growers of cannabis to desist from cannabis cultivation, plant cassava, yam, corn and other food crops.

“They themselves have confided in us that they are grateful for this initiative because even though there is more money in cannabis, cultivating food crops will give them peace of mind. So this is the new strategy and we are the first to use it in Africa. The United Nations Office of Drugs and Crime have welcomed it.

“The Federal Government of Nigeria has welcomed it as part of the Renewed Hope Agenda for illicit croppers to move away from crime to licit businesses,” he said.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

In his response, the Oba of Benin, Ewuare II, commended the NDLEA for its fight against illicit drugs and promised to personally submit his suggestions on the fight against drug abuse to the chairman.

“I must commend the NDLEA for their efforts to rid the society of illicit drugs and I will personally hand over my suggestions to the chairman,” he added.

The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council has said the education reforms introduced by President Bola Tinubu’s administration have resulted in the disbursement of N372.62bn in student loans and the training of 156,446 beneficiaries under the Technical and Vocational Education and Training programme.

The council, in a statement by its spokesperson and Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, on Wednesday, said the reforms had also improved access to basic education, strengthened teachers’ welfare and stabilised the academic calendar in tertiary institutions across the country.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

As the January 16, 2027, presidential election approaches, the achievements of President Bola Tinubu’s administration in over three years in office have come under intense criticism from opposition parties.

While some opposition figures have faulted the administration’s education reforms, others have dismissed its reported achievements, questioning their actual impact on Nigerians.

Reacting, APC PCC said the administration introduced free technical education covering tuition, boarding, textbooks and uniforms as part of efforts to strengthen vocational skills and expand employment opportunities.

The statement read, “President Bola Tinubu’s reforms in the education sector since assuming office have expanded access to learning, improved teachers’ welfare and stabilised the academic calendar across higher institutions in the country.

“According to the Federal Ministry of Education’s 2026 report on the Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative, the government’s interventions cover basic and secondary education, technical and vocational training, and tertiary education.

“The reforms focus on six priority areas: technical and vocational education, science and medical sciences, out-of-school children, girl-child education, digitalisation and education quality assurance.

“According to the NESRI report, the Federal Government allocated a record ₦3.52tn to education in the 2026 budget and secured $552m for the HOPE-EDU programme, which targets 29 million children, over 500,000 teachers and 65,000 public schools.”

The APC PCC stated that the BESDA programme had brought more than one million out-of-school children back into classrooms, trained 1,400 Tsangaya teachers and established 200 bilingual centres in 17 northern states.

It added that the AGILE programme had reached 7.19 million girls, including 3.7 million enrolled in secondary schools, while over 10,000 schools had received facility upgrades.

Alake explained that the President Tinubu administration introduced a revised national curriculum to reintroduce Nigerian History and strengthen Civic and Heritage Studies, adding that the National Learning Assessment had also been restored to monitor pupils’ performance and identify learning gaps.

The statement added, “Under EduRevamp, 53,553 teachers have registered, while 51,794 joined the first cohort of the Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway (ATPP), a six-month programme offering professional qualifications, certification and licensing.

“Backed by ₦2bn, the programme targets 250,000 teachers by 2027. Also, the Inspire Live initiative provides online lessons from Primary One to Senior Secondary School Three, supported by certified teachers and AI-assisted learning.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“Under President Tinubu’s administration, the TVET scheme has attracted over 2.8 million applications, with 156,446 verified trainees receiving free training, monthly stipends and start-up support.

“More than ₦65.7bn has already been disbursed to trainees, while another ₦30.2bn has gone to training centres. The government has also rehabilitated 38 technical colleges and introduced free technical education covering tuition, boarding, textbooks and uniforms.”

The APC PCC spokesperson said the Federal Government was investing N110bn in the rehabilitation of 18 federal medical schools across the six geopolitical zones.

He added that nursing enrolment increased from 81,480 in 2023 to 114,300 in 2025, while 20 STEM-focused tertiary institutions had been approved and 12 engineering and technology faculties earmarked for rehabilitation.

The APC PCC added that ,”NELFUND, a flagship programme of the Tinubu administration in the education sector, has processed 1,659,853 student loan applications and disbursed ₦372.62bn, comprising ₦192.89bn for tuition and ₦179.73bn for upkeep allowances across 319 tertiary institutions.

“The administration has resolved the age-long dispute between the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) and implemented the agreement providing for a 40 per cent increase in academic staff remuneration and improved welfare benefits.

“Additionally, the Tertiary Institutions Staff Support Fund has disbursed ₦28bn to 15,000 workers across 153 public institutions, offering eligible staff loans of up to ₦10m for housing, healthcare, transportation and education.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“Equally, the Federal Government has provided ₦365m annually for research and innovation through the National Laureate Prize, while the Student Venture Capital Grant has disbursed over ₦2.5bn to 45 student entrepreneurs. Each beneficiary can access up to ₦50m in equity-free funding.”

The Campaign Council also disclosed that entrepreneurship certification was ongoing in 14 federal universities, while the Diaspora BRIDGE initiative had registered 1,141 Nigerian professionals abroad, reaching 16,675 students in 107 tertiary institutions.

title: French blood storage impacted by freezer hacks as theories swirl about culprits
excerpt: French authorities say that fridges used in medical facilities to store blood for donations were impacted by recent cyber-attacks by unknown hackers.
description: French authorities say that fridges used in medical facilities to store blood for donations were impacted by recent cyber-attacks by unknown hackers.
content:
French authorities say that fridges used in medical facilities to store blood for donations were impacted by recent cyber-attacks by unknown hackers.

The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said cold rooms storing blood were impacted by hackers, with temperatures set to rise - but staff intervened to protect blood supplies.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

"No health impact has been identified and no loss of blood products is to be reported," the EFS said.

Up until now, only supermarkets were known to have been impacted by the hacks.

Meanwhile rumours have been circulating online about Russian hacktivist groups claiming they worked together to hack one of the systems that was used in the attacks which have affected European supermarkets.

Noname057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance posted that they successfully hacked Danfoss which led to speculation that they were the culprits behind the freezer hacks.

But analysts now question whether or not that meant they were behind the supermarket cyber-attacks.

While Russian groups are not being ruled out, experts say Iranian hacktivists or nation state hackers - or even teenagers pulling pranks - could also be the culprits.

Cyber-security researchers at multiple firms are pouring over evidence gathered from so-called "honeypots" to provide clues as to who is behind the waves of freezer hacks.

Three separate cyber-security firms have deployed fake freezer software traps to monitor how hackers attempt to use them for attacks.

In cyber-security, a "honeypot" is a digital decoy - such as a fake computer network or file - deliberately set up to look like a vulnerable target to lure and trap hackers.

By monitoring these traps, security experts can safely study an attacker's methods without putting real systems at risk.

According to activity gathered after the first wave of cyber-attacks, the second wave which hit several European countries was highly targeted.

"The fact that all these fridge freezers were hit simultaneously suggests planning and coordination," says Ryan Dewhurst from Spanish cyber-security company Previdian.

The entry point to the affected freezer software products was not difficult to exploit as they were poorly protected, with known attack methods already floating around online.

But experts like Dewhurst say the hacker or hackers had to gather the information about the devices' public IP addresses to create a target list then take time to plan which methods to use and when to execute them.

"Given the reported timing of when the devices had their temperatures increased, which seems to have been overnight for maximum damage - this is further evidence that the attack was planned and co-ordinated," he said.

Another cyber firm which has deployed similar honeypot tech to lure the hackers into revealing their tactics is Strathclyde-based Lupovis.

It had honeypots which appeared to be located around the world, and started seeing activity 10 days before the second wave of cyber-attacks.

Intriguingly, the team saw hackers scanning and probing their fake freezer sites only in Europe.

"We saw none of our honeypots in places like Africa or South America targeted at all," said Lupovis founder Dr Xavier Bellekens.

"Even pots in Ukraine were left alone."

A third company - French cyber-defence firm Sekoia - also noticed scanning activity prior to the second wave of cyber-attacks, but said it could have been automatic scanning without malicious intent.

In a report to its customers, it said evidence suggested the nature of the attack aligned with activity of Russian hacktivists or the Russian government, which is being accused of carrying out so-called "hybrid warfare" cyber-attacks across Europe.

But Sekoia's research also points to Iranian regime hackers or hacktivists too.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

"Iranian-aligned actors have an established record of targeting internet-exposed industrial control systems and previous incidents involved the same equipment in Israel and the US - both adversaries of Iran," the report said.

According to Sekoia, about 40 Israeli supermarkets running Danfoss controllers were compromised back in 2022.

Meanwhile in late August, freezers in at least six US military bases were forced into defrost mode, as in France. The controller models remain unconfirmed and investigations are ongoing.

"To date, we have no technical evidence indicating the involvement of Russian-speaking groups," a Sekoia spokesperson told the BBC.

"Furthermore, as NoName057 is not known to effectively conduct operations beyond DDoS attacks and has a history of making false attributions, we remain sceptical of their alleged claim of responsibility."

Distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks work by flooding a website or online service with internet traffic in an attempt to throw it offline, or otherwise make it inaccessible.

Authorities in several countries are actively investigating the hacks and warning supermarkets about potential future attacks.

But no formal attribution has been made.

None of the three cyber firms which have been gathering honey pot data are ruling out that it could be a teenager.

But with the degree of planning necessary the experts all agree it would have to be a well co-ordinated group - and if so, they would expect online bragging to surface soon.

Sekoia also said the possibility remains that all three waves could have been carried out by different and distinct groups or copycats.

content:
Former Super Eagles striker, Victor Anichebe, is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire English League One club Bromley, in what could mark his first major investment in football club ownership.

According to talkSPORT on Wednesday, the 38-year-old is leading a wealthy African group of investors negotiating with Bromley’s owner, Robin Stanton-Gleaves, over a possible takeover.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The discussions are said to be progressing, with both parties working towards reaching an agreement.

The proposed acquisition comes at a challenging period for Bromley, who are struggling in their first season in League One following successive promotions from the National League in 2024 and League Two last season.

The club’s recent run of results has also raised concerns about its ability to retain its League One status.

Anichebe’s proposed takeover could provide fresh investment and a new direction as the South London club seeks to improve its position.

The former Everton striker has developed an interest in sports investment since retiring from professional football in 2018.

He is the founder and owner of Lumira Group, an investment company with interests in sports, education, healthcare and infrastructure in the United Kingdom.

Anichebe was also recently linked to a proposed £20m leisure development project in Liverpool.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

His interest in Bromley follows an earlier attempt to acquire non-league club Gateshead last year, although the proposed deal did not materialise.

During his playing career, Anichebe featured in the Premier League, scoring 27 goals and providing 12 assists.

At international level, he made 11 appearances for Nigeria’s senior national team, scoring once.

His only goal for the Super Eagles came in a 3-0 friendly victory over Kenya in 2011.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He was also part of Nigeria’s Under-23 team that won silver at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, scoring against Japan during the tournament.

If completed, the Bromley acquisition would represent a significant step in Anichebe’s transition from professional football to club ownership and sports investment.

excerpt: Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the Allied Peoples Movement presidential candidate and Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has unveiled his Reset Agenda manif...
description: Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the Allied Peoples Movement presidential candidate and Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has unveiled his Reset Agenda manif...
content:
Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the Allied Peoples Movement presidential candidate and Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has unveiled his Reset Agenda manifesto, promising reforms in the economy, education, security and the political system.

Speaking on Wednesday in Abuja during the presentation of the manifesto, Makinde said his ambition was driven by the need to address Nigeria’s challenges and restore the vision of its founding fathers.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

He said his proposed administration would prioritise policies that improve living conditions, expand opportunities and strengthen public institutions.

“My simple proposition is that government must make life easier for the people. We must develop people’s abilities and expand their access to opportunities. We must also have institutions that work,” he said.

Makinde stressed that government promises must be backed by clear implementation plans, measurable targets and accountable institutions.

He identified the disconnect between macroeconomic reforms and improvements in citizens’ living conditions as one of the major challenges confronting the country.

“For us, macroeconomic reforms must translate into improvements in people’s lives. What does macroeconomic stability mean if it does not improve the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians?” he asked.

On the economy, the governor proposed a system through which Nigerians would benefit from increased crude oil revenues, arguing that additional earnings above government budget benchmarks should translate into improved public welfare.

He also promised measurable performance targets within his administration’s first 100 days and called for accountability in government spending.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

On electricity, Makinde urged Nigerians to hold the Federal Government accountable for its promise to improve power supply, insisting that it must continue to address challenges in generation and distribution despite the electricity autonomy law.

Addressing the political system, he proposed that presidential candidates should secure at least 51 per cent of votes to win elections, arguing that the requirement would encourage broader political cooperation.

He also proposed a transitional government of national unity and a national conference to discuss the country’s challenges and agree on a common direction.

His running mate, Lawal Musa Daura, criticised the suppression of opposition parties, saying a level playing field was essential to sustaining democracy.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He said a vibrant opposition complemented the government and helped reduce political tensions.

Daura identified education, the economy, security and the socio-political system as the four pillars of the Reset Agenda, pledging that their proposed administration would prioritise national interests over personal gains.

title: 2027: Obi condemns attack on convoy in C’River
excerpt: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has condemned an attack on his campaign convoy by suspected thugs in Calabar, Cross River State, assuri...
description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has condemned an attack on his campaign convoy by suspected thugs in Calabar, Cross River State, assuri...
content:
The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has condemned an attack on his campaign convoy by suspected thugs in Calabar, Cross River State, assuring supporters that political violence would not be allowed to undermine the 2027 general election.

Obi spoke at a town hall meeting in Calabar on Wednesday, hours after his convoy reportedly came under attack, with suspected assailants smashing the windscreens and side mirrors of some campaign buses.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

A viral 30-second video of the incident showed some of the attackers, mostly dressed in black shirts, fez caps and face coverings, using machetes to damage vehicles in the convoy.

The attack reportedly caused panic as passersby and roadside traders fled the scene.

One of Obi’s media aides, Esther Umoh, had raised the alarm in a post on her official X account.

“Thugs are trying to attack our convoy,” she wrote.

Shortly afterwards, Umoh shared another five-second video showing a victim with a gunshot injury to the leg being evacuated from the scene. She attributed the injury to a stray bullet.

Speaking at the town hall meeting, Obi recounted how he witnessed the attack and said his security team advised him to take another route after the assailants allegedly armed themselves with machetes and other weapons.

He said, “They were throwing stones, and I saw people running back. And my security people said we should find another way because they have machetes and other things.

“I asked, ‘In Nigeria? I am coming down to go and meet them.’ By the time they saw what was happening, they left. All these things happened because Nigerians allow it. We are not going to allow it in 2027.”

The former Anambra State governor arrived in Calabar alongside his wife, Margaret, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, for the town hall meeting.

Efforts to reach the spokesperson for the NDC Presidential Campaign Council, Constance Ikokwu, and Obi’s spokesman, Idris Zekeri, for further comments were unsuccessful.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The incident is the latest reported security challenge involving Obi’s campaign, coming about two months after his convoy encountered a blockade and confrontation with youths in Benue State.

During the Benue visit, Obi’s convoy was blocked by youths along the Makurdi-Gboko Federal Highway as he travelled to the state for political engagements ahead of the 2027 presidential election and to commiserate with victims of the June 2025 attacks in Yelewata.

Trouble reportedly started a few metres from the airport when the convoy encountered a roadblock mounted by the youths, who prevented motorists from using the two-lane highway.

The blockade caused traffic congestion, while the police were criticised for failing to disperse the youths promptly.

The Benue State Commissioner of Police, Cletus Nwadiogbu, subsequently disclosed that no fewer than 46 suspects had been arrested in connection with the incident.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Nwadiogbu said investigations were ongoing and that security operatives were trailing key leaders of the youths.

He warned that the police would not tolerate political intolerance as the country approached the 2027 general election.

content:
UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has dismissed suggestions that the growing political influence of former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, could threaten Governor Alex Otti’s re-election chances in 2027, insisting that the governor enjoys sufficient grassroots support to secure another term.

The party said the political momentum behind Otti, which it described as the “Otti wave”, was strong enough to withstand opposition and guarantee victory for the Labour Party in the state.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

There have been suggestions that Obi’s popularity and influence played a significant role in Otti’s victory in the 2023 governorship election and could again determine the outcome of the 2027 poll.

However, the Publicity Secretary of the Labour Party in Abia, Chief Emenike Iroegbu, said the party had established a strong grassroots presence across markets, motor parks, local government areas and wards, making it confident of winning all elective positions in the state.

Speaking in Umuahia, Iroegbu acknowledged Obi’s political stature but maintained that his influence would not undermine the Labour Party’s position in Abia.

He noted that Otti had remained in the Labour Party while the party continued to strengthen its political structures across the state’s 184 wards and 17 local government areas.

“What is currently driving political support for the Labour Party in Abia is the ‘Otti wave’. The ‘Otti wave’ is strong enough to withstand any opposition ahead of the 2027 polls. This is the ‘Otti wave’ that has been spreading like wildfire in the 17 LGAs of Abia State,” he said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Iroegbu claimed that candidates of other political parties, including the National Democratic Congress (NDC), All Progressives Congress (APC) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), had been associating themselves with Otti’s popularity through campaign posters and social media posts.

He added that the influence of the former Anambra governor was not strong enough to weaken the Labour Party’s political base in Abia.

The party spokesman also expressed confidence that its grassroots structures would translate into electoral victories across the state in 2027.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

On the inclusion of politicians who served in previous administrations in the party’s campaign structures, Iroegbu defended the move, saying political parties should remain open to individuals willing to join and contribute to governance.

He argued that admitting such politicians into the Labour Party did not represent a departure from the principles and policies of the Otti administration, insisting that the governor remained firmly in control of his government.

title: Senate advances Agricultural Revolution Bill
excerpt: ABUJA — A bill seeking to establish a comprehensive legal framework for the transformation and modernisation of Nigeria’s agricultural sector has scaled second reading in the Se...
description: ABUJA — A bill seeking to establish a comprehensive legal framework for the transformation and modernisation of Nigeria’s agricultural sector has scaled second reading in the Se...
content:
ABUJA — A bill seeking to establish a comprehensive legal framework for the transformation and modernisation of Nigeria’s agricultural sector has scaled second reading in the Senate.

The bill, sponsored by the Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau (APC, Kano North), seeks to promote food security, agricultural productivity, mechanisation, irrigation, agricultural financing, agro-industrialisation, rural development and climate-resilient farming.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Following its passage at second reading, the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, referred the proposed legislation to the Senate Committees on Agricultural Production, Services and Rural Development, and Agricultural Colleges and Institutions for further legislative consideration.

Akpabio directed the committees to report back to the Senate within four weeks.

The bill, titled, A Bill for an Act to Provide a Comprehensive Legal Framework for the Transformation and Modernisation of Agriculture in Nigeria, is also designed to promote sustainable agricultural development and address longstanding challenges in the sector.

Leading the debate on its general principles, Barau lamented that agriculture, which was once the mainstay of Nigeria’s economy, was no longer performing optimally.

He recalled that between the 1950s and early 1980s, agricultural production supported numerous industries, including textile and processing companies in Lagos, Kano and Port Harcourt.

He regretted that several industries, particularly those in Kano’s Sharada and Bompai industrial areas, which once supported vibrant economic activities, had become largely dormant.

Barau also recalled that the Second Republic government introduced the Green Revolution Programme but noted that its implementation lacked an enabling legal framework.

According to him, the absence of legislation made it difficult to sustain the programme beyond the administration that introduced it.

He said Nigeria had the human and natural resources required to transform agriculture but lacked effective mechanisms to harness the sector’s enormous potential.

“The bill is to provoke conversation, bring in our expertise to look at the entire scenario and see how we can change the trajectory,” he said.

Barau urged senators to consider the proposed legislation from the perspective of patriotism rather than partisan politics, stressing the need for collective action to reposition the agricultural sector.

Contributing, the Senate Whip, Senator Mohammed Monguno (APC, Borno North), said the bill would translate Nigeria’s economic diversification policy from oil dependence to agriculture into practical reality.

He said agriculture contributed about 40 per cent of Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product and provided approximately 70 per cent of employment.

Monguno, however, lamented that Nigeria had consistently fallen short of agricultural budgetary allocation targets, with its highest allocation in recent years standing at approximately five per cent.

He said the proposed legislation would address challenges relating to mechanisation, agricultural financing, rural infrastructure and post-harvest losses through a comprehensive legal framework.

Also contributing, Senator Babangida Hussaini (APC, Jigawa North-West) commended the bill’s sponsor, noting that his contribution was informed by his experience as a practising farmer.

Hussaini recalled that despite the introduction of the Agricultural Credit Guarantee Scheme in 1976, Nigeria had yet to establish sustainable agricultural financing mechanisms.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He said the bill would harmonise agricultural policies and programmes while addressing challenges across production, financing, marketing, storage and processing.

The senator cited Jigawa’s production of hibiscus and sesame seeds, lamenting that inadequate storage, marketing and processing facilities had prevented farmers from maximising the economic potential of the commodities.

He also urged the Senate to pay adequate attention to livestock production, describing it as a significant economic opportunity.

In his contribution, Senator Anthony Ani (APC, Ebonyi South) described the bill as comprehensive, saying it addressed virtually every aspect of agricultural production.

He identified mechanisation, irrigation, research, innovation, extension services, financing and support for women, youths and small-scale farmers as key provisions of the proposed legislation.

Ani said the bill would help address challenges confronting farmers, including climate change, inadequate farming equipment and poor agricultural infrastructure.

Similarly, Senator Adeniyi Adegbonmire (APC, Ondo Central) supported the bill, describing the proposed legal framework as necessary to ensure continuity in Nigeria’s agricultural development policies.

He said the legislation would establish a National Agricultural Revolution Programme with clearly defined national targets and implementation strategies.

According to him, the framework would place successive administrations under statutory obligations to sustain established agricultural development programmes.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Adegbonmire also recalled that the Green Revolution Programme introduced in 1976 lacked an enabling law, making it vulnerable to discontinuation by subsequent administrations.

He described the proposed legislation as far-reaching, noting that it would provide a statutory framework for coordinating agricultural development, financing and other interventions.

title: Oyebanji warns commissioners against arrogance, corruption
excerpt: ADO-EKITI — Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has warned newly inaugurated commissioners and special advisers against arrogance, indiscipline, corruption and abuse of offic...
description: ADO-EKITI — Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has warned newly inaugurated commissioners and special advisers against arrogance, indiscipline, corruption and abuse of offic...
content:
ADO-EKITI — Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has warned newly inaugurated commissioners and special advisers against arrogance, indiscipline, corruption and abuse of office, declaring that his administration would not tolerate unethical conduct or inefficiency.

He charged the appointees to remain humble, accountable and committed to delivering quality service to the people, warning that bureaucratic delays and careless mistakes capable of undermining the state’s development agenda would not be condoned.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Oyebanji gave the warning on Wednesday in Ado-Ekiti during the inauguration of three commissioners and 10 special advisers into the State Executive Council.

The new commissioners are Dayo Apata, SAN, Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice; Akintunde Oyebode, Commissioner for Finance; and Dr Oyebanji Filani, Commissioner for Health and Human Services.

The 10 special advisers are Prof. James Olaleye, e-GIS, Lands and Survey; James Folorunso, Bureau of Public Procurement; Dr John Moyo Ekundayo, Office of Transformation, Strategy and Delivery; Bunmi Talabi, Bureau of Special Projects; and Olayinka Oyebode, Chief Press Secretary and Special Adviser on Media.

Others are Princess Adetoun Agboola, Special Education and Social Inclusion; Dr Gbenga Oyewole, Development Planning and Budget; Kayode Adaramodu, Economic Affairs and Private Sector Development; Ebenezer Boluwade, Agriculture and Food Security; and Prof. Akeem Azeez, Special Duties.

The governor said the inauguration, coming barely two weeks after the swearing-in of the Secretary to the State Government and other key officials, was aimed at ensuring that his second-term administration commenced without delay.

He said the second term was not an opportunity for complacency or self-indulgence but a period to consolidate the achievements of the first term and accelerate the state’s development.

Oyebanji particularly cautioned returning commissioners against allowing their experience and length of service to create a false sense of indispensability.

“I would also like to counsel you to resist the temptation of the illusion of invincibility and indispensability, which could ultimately breed arrogance. At the end of the day, only God is truly indispensable.

“We must all therefore remain gracious and wholeheartedly dedicated to our unwavering service to the good people of Ekiti State,” he said.

He declared that he would be impatient and intolerant of indiscipline, unethical behaviour and corruption, insisting that all government activities must reflect professionalism, transparency, technical competence and efficiency.

Identifying discipline and speed as the two principles that would drive his administration, the governor urged the appointees to ensure that policies and projects were implemented promptly and in accordance with global best practices.

“We must work very hard to successfully translate all electoral promises into visible, concrete and life-changing outcomes for the citizens. We must always remember that behind every single vote cast in our favour stands a deeply rooted hope and legitimate expectations,” he said.

Oyebanji also charged members of the Executive Council to work as a united team, support one another and avoid actions capable of creating divisions within government.

He warned against the emergence of what he described as “untouchable imperial lords or bureaucratic dictators”, irrespective of how long any official had occupied a particular position.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The governor expressed confidence in the competence of the returning commissioners, particularly Oyebode, Apata and Filani, saying their reappointment reflected his recognition of their contributions and confidence in their ability to deliver.

He noted that Oyebode and Filani had distinguished themselves nationally, with the former serving as chairman of the Forum of Commissioners of Finance and the latter having chaired the forum of health commissioners.

According to him, their continued presence in the cabinet would provide institutional stability, continuity and valuable experience, adding that they were expected to resume work immediately without unnecessary learning curves.

He urged the returning appointees to bring renewed energy, creativity, maturity and commitment to their responsibilities.

Oyebanji also welcomed the newly appointed special advisers, describing them as accomplished professionals and technocrats selected to strengthen the administration’s capacity to deliver on its development agenda.

He assured them of his support, saying their appointments reflected his commitment to bringing competent people into government, irrespective of where they were found.

The governor thanked the families and friends of the appointees for attending the ceremony, urging them to support the officials through prayers and understanding rather than placing unnecessary pressure on them.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“Public office is a trust, and we must help to strengthen the trust imposed in them and not betray it,” he said.

Responding on behalf of the new executive members, Apata commended the governor for the confidence reposed in them and the opportunity to serve the state in his second term.

description: The United Nations Children’s Fund has reported five poliovirus detections in Niger State, comprising three samples from humans and two from environmental surveillance, raising ...
content:
The United Nations Children’s Fund has reported five poliovirus detections in Niger State, comprising three samples from humans and two from environmental surveillance, raising concerns over the continued circulation of the virus.

The agency urged residents to strengthen surveillance, community sensitisation and routine immunisation to prevent further spread and help the state achieve polio-free status.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

UNICEF disclosed this on Wednesday during a mass mobilisation dialogue organised in collaboration with the Niger State Primary Health Care Development Agency.

The agency’s representative, Mrs Grace Odeyemi, said the virus was detected in Bida and Chanchaga Local Government Areas, calling for increased surveillance and compliance with polio vaccination.

She urged parents to ensure their children received the vaccine and encouraged community leaders to support awareness campaigns.

Odeyemi explained that health workers monitored children with symptoms of paralysis and collected samples for laboratory testing to determine whether the condition was caused by poliovirus or another illness.

“We still carry out routine immunisation of the population. We are vaccinating the children to ensure that we eradicate the disease from the state. We sample humans, that is, any child that we find in the community with paralysis, having a similar feature to polio-affected victims.

“We quickly notify our local surveillance officers to collect samples for tests to see if it is polio or something else that is actually causing the paralysis because it’s not only the polio virus that causes paralysis,” she said.

She added that environmental surveillance was also used to detect the virus in samples collected from the surroundings, even where no human case had been identified.

“We detected the virus in Chanchaga and also in Bida. The virus is still circulating within our environment where we collected the sample.

“So, we have one reported in Chanchaga and the second one was also found from environmental sampling in Bida, LG, making a total of five polio detections we have in the state, three from human and two from environmental sampling,” she said.

The Niger State Immunisation Officer, Abubakar Usman, also confirmed the five detections, saying the state had introduced routine and reactive vaccination to protect children and contain the spread.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

“The virus was detected in the state. We found three from human and two from environmental sampling and a lot of strategies have been put in place to curtail the spread of these diseases. We did reactive vaccination, that is, we promptly reacted to vaccinate other children within those areas where those viruses were actually found,” he said.

Usman said health officials had also engaged community leaders and other intervention groups to educate residents on the importance of immunisation.

He attributed the continued circulation of the virus to poor routine immunisation and vaccine hesitancy in some communities.

“All of this is as a result of what? Poor routine immunisation. The virus is here and it is as a result of a high level of non-compliance. This is just a drop in the ocean. We are able to see this because it’s a campaign. We have to go out to actually act rather than the concept of the mother to bring their child for vaccination compared to routine immunisation that is voluntary,” he added.

The latest detections came months after Niger State reported three new polio cases in Magama and Mariga Local Government Areas, prompting the state government to intensify surveillance and community sensitisation.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

In June 2026, health authorities, in collaboration with UNICEF and other partners, also organised engagements with traditional and religious leaders to strengthen efforts to prevent the spread of the virus.
Nigeria was certified free of wild poliovirus in August 2020, but circulating variant poliovirus remains a public health concern, particularly in communities with low immunisation coverage.

The World Health Organisation has continued to call for stronger routine vaccination and surveillance to prevent further transmission.

title: NMDPRA warns of risks from Ogun illegal refinery
excerpt: …EFCC traces discovery to whistleblower’s tip, surveillance
description: …EFCC traces discovery to whistleblower’s tip, surveillance
content:
…EFCC traces discovery to whistleblower’s tip, surveillance

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) has warned that products from an illegal refinery uncovered in Ogere-Remo, Ikenne Local Government Area of Ogun State, could pose serious risks to vehicles, automobile engines and public safety.

The authority gave the warning on Wednesday during an inspection of the facility jointly conducted with operatives of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

The Ogun State Coordinator of NMDPRA, Dr Atilola Akinyemi, said the facility, which occupies more than three hectares of land, had no operating licence or permit from any regulatory agency and was operating outside the supervision of relevant authorities.

He disclosed that the facility had an underground storage tank with an estimated capacity of more than 90,000 litres.

Akinyemi described the installation as a crude and illegal operation, saying its structures and equipment appeared designed to replicate the processes of a conventional refinery without complying with the required regulatory, technical and safety standards.

“The facility you see here is very crude and completely illegal. This is not a refinery by any standard. This facility does not have a permit from any regulatory authority, and its operations are unknown to the relevant authorities,” he said.

He explained that intelligence gathering by the EFCC was instrumental to the discovery, noting that routine regulatory monitoring alone might not have exposed an operation of such magnitude.

“This kind of discovery cannot be made through ordinary monitoring alone; it requires intelligence gathering. As the Zonal Director of the EFCC has explained, intelligence was instrumental in uncovering this operation. We need more of such efforts,” he said.

According to him, preliminary investigations showed that the facility had designated sections for receiving feedstock, storage, heating, processing and cooling.

Other installations discovered during the inspection included underground heating systems, water hydrants for cooling, locally fabricated storage tanks, separation silos and other equipment used in petroleum processing.

Akinyemi likened the operation to illegal refining activities that characterised parts of the Niger Delta in the 1990s and early 2000s, questioning the source of the crude materials allegedly being processed at the facility.

“One question that comes to mind is: where do they source their feedstock?” he queried.

He said the equipment and general layout suggested that the operators had some technical knowledge but had established the facility outside the country’s petroleum regulatory framework.

The NMDPRA coordinator cautioned against identifying the recovered products as diesel or Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) based solely on their physical appearance.

He said laboratory analysis was necessary to determine their chemical composition and establish whether they met the required standards for automotive use.

“When we examine their final product, it may look like diesel to the average person. However, we cannot classify it as diesel or Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) until laboratory tests have been conducted to establish its actual composition,” he said.

Akinyemi warned that releasing unverified products into the domestic market could damage vehicles and automobile engines.

“Imagine what would happen if these products found their way into the market. Vehicles, automobiles and their engines would be exposed to serious risks,” he added.

He confirmed that the recovered petroleum products and materials had been confiscated and placed in the custody of the Federal Government in accordance with applicable regulations.

He also pledged that the authority would sustain its collaboration with security and law enforcement agencies to identify and dismantle other illegal petroleum processing facilities across the state.

Akinyemi commended the EFCC and other participating agencies, saying intelligence sharing and coordinated enforcement were critical to tackling illegal activities in the petroleum sector.

Meanwhile, the EFCC Zonal Director, Lagos Zonal Directorate 2, Bawa Usman Kaltungo, said the operation followed information provided by a Nigerian whistleblower.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He said the commission conducted surveillance to verify the information before launching a sting operation that led to the discovery of the facility.

According to Kaltungo, the whistleblower responded to an appeal by the EFCC Executive Chairman, who had encouraged members of the public to report suspicious activities under the commission’s whistleblowing policy.

“A Nigerian who responded to that call subsequently provided us with information about an illegal mining site. We informed the Chairman, who directed us to conduct surveillance first. We carried out the surveillance and confirmed that the information was accurate,” he said.

He added that the EFCC chairman subsequently authorised the sting operation, during which the facility was uncovered.

“We are also on the verge of discovering another location,” Kaltungo said.

He further disclosed that the commission was investigating the ownership structure of companies allegedly linked to the operation, adding that some of their ultimate beneficial owners were reportedly based in China.

Also speaking during the inspection, the EFCC Director of Operations, Gbolahan Latona, warned that illegal petroleum processing activities could undermine legitimate investments in Nigeria’s refining industry and deprive the country of revenue.

Latona said the commission would ensure that assets established to be proceeds of crime were recovered and put to productive use in accordance with the law.

He cited the conversion of Nok University, following its forfeiture to the government, into the Federal University of Applied Sciences, Kachia, as an example of the commission’s asset recovery and social reuse initiative.

He said the facility in Ogere-Remo could also be subjected to appropriate recovery and reuse procedures, depending on the outcome of investigations and the necessary legal processes.

Latona warned that illegal operators must not be allowed to undermine investments by legitimate players in the petroleum industry, particularly major domestic refining projects.

He said the arrested suspects would be prosecuted if sufficient evidence was established against them.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The commission, he added, would extend its investigations to individuals and interests allegedly financing the operation from outside Nigeria.

At the end of the inspection, NMDPRA officials sealed the facility.

“Our democracy is strengthened when all parties submit to lawful processes, and I enjoin all supporters, party faithful, and citizens of Nasarawa State to remain calm, peaceful, and law-abiding as we study the details of the judgment with our legal team. Angbazo maintained that his political ambition was driven by the interests of the people of Nasarawa State, particularly their security, prosperity and welfare, rather than personal considerations.

He reaffirmed his commitment to the ideals of the ADC, describing the party as a platform for providing a credible, inclusive and people-oriented alternative for the state.

…Ezeobi says 442km asphalted, less than 5km affected by failures

The Anambra State Government has awarded contracts for the construction of 908.44 kilometres of roads across the state since Governor Chukwuma Soludo assumed office in 2022, the Commissioner for Works, Architect Okey Ezeobi, has said.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Ezeobi, who disclosed this while addressing journalists in Awka, said 442 kilometres of the roads had been fully asphalted, describing the administration’s road construction programme as unprecedented in the state’s history.

He claimed that the combined road construction achievements of the three previous governors fell short of the number of kilometres asphalted by the Soludo administration.

According to him, the government has awarded 143 road contracts since taking office.

Addressing complaints on social media about the condition of some roads constructed by the administration, the commissioner said the affected portions amounted to less than five kilometres out of the 442 kilometres asphalted.

“Of all the 442 kilometres of road we have asphalted, if you cut the portions that failed as a result of the effects of underground water, they are not up to five kilometres. That means that we have over 95 per cent of all the roads constructed by this administration in perfect condition,” he said.

Ezeobi attributed some of the reported road failures to underground water, unusually heavy rainfall and blocked drainage channels, insisting that the government was addressing the affected sections.

He alleged that some residents deliberately blocked drainage channels to allow sand to accumulate for harvesting and commercial sale, thereby worsening flooding and damaging public infrastructure.

The commissioner explained that some roads remained in good condition until the recent heavy rainy season, which he said exposed the effects of underground water that had not been adequately captured in the initial construction data.

“Many of the roads were designed and built and they never became bad until this year’s heavy rainy season. It’s the underground water that is the cause of the road damage, as the data we used did not capture the volume of the underground water,” he said.

He added that the effects of underground water were also visible in residential buildings, where ground-floor surfaces were reportedly peeling.

On allegations of poor construction standards and the engagement of unqualified contractors, Ezeobi maintained that the government had carefully selected reputable construction firms to handle its projects.

He described the contractors as A-rated companies, saying they had the capacity to return to sites and carry out reconstruction whenever defects occurred.

According to him, the affected contractors were undertaking the repairs at no additional cost to the state government.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He, however, acknowledged that human errors could not be completely ruled out as a possible cause of some road failures.

The commissioner cited the Amawbia-Ekwulobia dual carriageway as one of the roads facing challenges because of erosion-prone sections and swampy areas where underground water frequently rises.

He said the volume of rainfall recorded this year was unprecedented in the past 50 years, adding that floodwater had seeped underground and affected road infrastructure, including some Federal Government projects.

Ezeobi disclosed that the government planned to remove damaged asphalt in affected areas and undertake cement-based stabilisation to prevent further damage from underground water.

He said the process would begin after the underground water had sufficiently drained, after which the stabilised sections would be allowed to set before fresh asphalt was applied.

The commissioner assured residents that the government remained committed to delivering quality roads, adding that the ongoing reconstruction was deliberate and would not attract additional costs to the state.

He dismissed some social media criticisms of the state’s road projects as politically motivated, arguing that the comments did not reflect the actual situation on the ground.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Ezeobi said the government would formally announce the completion and certification of the affected roads before their official reopening to motorists.

He added that the administration was working to ensure that roads across the state were motorable before the Christmas season.

The police arrested one suspect in connection with the attack.

The Police Public Relations Officer in the state, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, who confirmed the arrest in a statement made available to journalists in Calabar, said the suspect, identified as Victor Edet Yellow-Duke, 27, had been apprehended, while investigations had commenced to identify those behind the attack and their sponsors.

“NDC supporters under heavy attack in Watt Market. The police have made an arrest to this effect. The suspect name is Victor Edet Yellow Duke, male, 27 years,” the police spokesman said.

He assured residents that normalcy had been restored and that adequate security had been deployed to strategic locations in the metropolis to prevent a recurrence.

The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the dismissal of three senior police officers and the demotion of 16 others over various cases of misconduct.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The commission also approved severe reprimands for 21 officers and ordinary reprimands for two others, bringing the number of officers sanctioned to 42.

However, three officers were exonerated, while some previously suspended officers were reinstated into the Nigeria Police Force.

The decisions were reached at the commission’s plenary meeting presided over by its Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (retd.), at the Solomon Arase Conference Hall, the commission’s corporate headquarters in Abuja.

A statement by the PSC spokesman, Torty Njoku, said the disciplinary actions followed established cases of serious misconduct and conduct unbecoming of officers of the law.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Reaffirming the commission’s zero tolerance for corruption, human rights abuses, interference in land and civil matters, and other forms of misconduct in the police force, Argungu assured Nigerians that disciplinary cases before the commission would continue to receive speedy attention.

The chairman commended the Chairman of the PSC Standing Committee on Discipline and Legal Matters, Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (retd.), and other board members for their contributions to the consideration of the disciplinary cases and appeals.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Those commended included DIG (Dr) Taiwo Lakanu (retd.), Justice Christine Dabup, Alhaji Abdulfatah Mohammed, the Secretary to the Commission, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani, and the Director of the Police Discipline Department, Mr Ferdinand U. Ekpe.

Argungu acknowledged their dedication throughout the departmental, committee and plenary consideration of the cases.

Google was met with swift backlash on Tuesday after it announced that schools using Google’s K-12 software will not be able to use Search unless they opt in to using AI tools.

Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told The New York Times that “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” so if a student’s school doesn’t opt in to using AI tools like Gemini, then students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”

---

Even as Google made this announcement on a busy Election Day, several left-leaning politicians took time to speak up about their concerns.

Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT) accused Google in an X post of “extortion,” writing that “Google is threatening schools: if you stop your students from using AI, we will cut off your access to Google Search.” Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) said on X  that Google is “more concerned with forcing Gemini into schools than enabling students to succeed.”

President Trump claimed that AI oligarchs could regulate themselves because they “love our country.” Now, Google is threatening schools: if you stop your students from using AI, we will cut off your access to Google Search. That’s not love. That’s extortion. PAUSE AI NOW.

Lina Khan, the former FTC chair and staunch advocate against monopolies, also condemned Google’s decision as anti-competitive.

“This highlights the danger of allowing an unregulated monopolist to control an essential service,” she wrote. “Multiple courts have found Google liable for violating antitrust laws, and this latest move shows it remains unchastened.”

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google of being a monopoly, commenting, “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children.”

Google is using its search monopoly to coerce schools into adopting AI. This highlights the danger of allowing an unregulated monopolist to control an essential service. While Search is a necessary tool for information gathering, educators worry that its built-in AI overviews could dissuade students from finding answers themselves. For millions of students required to use Chromebooks and Google education tools, using a different search engine isn’t a simple fix.

Google says that it’s working on a “Guided Learning” tool for student accounts in Search, which is supposed to walk students through the process of solving a problem or finding information, rather than just handing them the answer. If a student is struggling with a math problem, for example, the feature may prompt them to refresh their memory about the rules for dividing exponents, instead of spitting out a number.
