title: Senate proposes six-month jail term for hospitals denying emergency care
excerpt: ABUJA — The Senate has passed for second reading a bill seeking to make it compulsory for public and private hospitals across Nigeria to provide emergency medical treatment, pre...
description: ABUJA — The Senate has passed for second reading a bill seeking to make it compulsory for public and private hospitals across Nigeria to provide emergency medical treatment, pre...
content:
ABUJA — The Senate has passed for second reading a bill seeking to make it compulsory for public and private hospitals across Nigeria to provide emergency medical treatment, prescribing up to six months’ imprisonment for facilities and individuals who violate its provisions.

The proposed legislation also prescribes a fine of up to ₦300,000, imprisonment for six months, or both, for anyone convicted of denying emergency medical treatment.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The bill, sponsored by Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua (APC, Katsina Central), seeks to amend the National Health Act, 2014, to establish mandatory emergency medical treatment standards and referral protocols in healthcare facilities.

Titled, “A Bill for an Act to Amend the National Health Act, 2014 to Provide for Emergency Medical Treatment Standards and Referral Protocols in Healthcare Facilities; and for Related Matters, 2026” (SB. 759), it was referred to the Senate Committee on Health (Secondary and Tertiary) for further legislative action, with a directive to report back in four weeks.

Under the proposed amendment, no healthcare provider, health worker or medical establishment would be allowed to deny anyone emergency medical treatment for any reason.

It also requires healthcare professionals to commence life-saving interventions, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation, airway management and bleeding control, immediately after identifying a life-threatening condition.

The bill proposes that hospitals conduct triage and initial assessments within 15 minutes of a patient’s arrival, while basic stabilisation measures, including oxygen administration, intravenous fluids, pain management and initial diagnostic procedures, must begin within 30 minutes.

For patients requiring admission, hospital beds are to be assigned within two hours, subject to availability.

Where beds are unavailable, healthcare facilities would be required to commence immediate stabilisation and arrange the patient’s transfer to another hospital.

The proposed legislation further requires hospitals to initiate referral arrangements within two hours and complete the transfer process within three hours of a patient’s arrival, except where circumstances beyond their control prevent compliance.

It also mandates hospitals to dispatch an ambulance or arrange alternative transportation within 30 minutes of communicating a referral decision.

Beyond emergency response timelines, the bill seeks to introduce mandatory emergency care training and certification for healthcare workers, with recertification intervals not exceeding 18 months.

It also mandates the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria to jointly develop a standardised national emergency care curriculum.

However, healthcare practitioners would be protected from penalties where resource constraints prevent compliance, provided the challenges are properly documented and prescribed referral procedures are followed.

Leading debate on the bill, Yar’Adua said the proposed amendment would address critical gaps in Nigeria’s healthcare system by establishing enforceable standards for emergency treatment and referral procedures.

He said it would guarantee timely and life-saving medical attention to Nigerians during emergencies, irrespective of their social status, wealth, influence or location.

According to him, preventable deaths persist because many healthcare facilities lack clearly defined and enforceable timelines for patient assessment, stabilisation and treatment.

He cited Nigeria’s contribution to approximately 10 per cent of global maternal deaths, attributing part of the problem to delays in accessing emergency obstetric care.

Yar’Adua said the proposed legislation would strengthen coordination among primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare facilities, while ensuring that patients are stabilised before being referred to other hospitals.

He added that the bill would protect healthcare workers acting in good faith within documented resource limitations while ensuring accountability for wilful negligence.

The senator said the proposed amendment was consistent with international practices, citing Ghana, South Africa, Kenya, the United Kingdom and the United States.

Supporting the bill, the Senate Whip, Senator Mohammed Monguno (APC, Borno North), said it would address deaths arising from road accidents and maternal emergencies.

He lamented that some healthcare providers neglected emergency patients, resulting in avoidable deaths, and said the proposed amendment would introduce criminal liability for such negligence.

Monguno said the legislation would address gaps in the existing National Health Act and reinforce government’s responsibility to protect the welfare of citizens.

Similarly, Senator Diket Plang (Plateau Central) said the bill would improve emergency admissions and establish appropriate referral procedures across different levels of healthcare delivery.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He noted that rural communities particularly needed the intervention because childbirth complications often required urgent referrals from primary healthcare centres to higher-level facilities.

Plang stressed that patients must be stabilised before transportation, adding that the proposed provisions would help prevent avoidable deaths during emergency transfers.

However, Senator Francis Faduyile (APC, Ondo South) cautioned against criminalising healthcare professionals without first addressing inadequate facilities, personnel shortages and other systemic challenges.

He said many hospitals lacked sufficient doctors, oxygen cylinders and emergency equipment, making it difficult for healthcare workers to meet the proposed timelines.

Faduyile questioned how a doctor attending to several patients simultaneously could be held criminally responsible when another emergency case arrived.

He also raised concerns about inadequate funding, noting that private healthcare providers frequently attended to emergency patients without receiving reimbursement for the services.

The senator argued that Nigeria’s healthcare challenges required a comprehensive review of the National Health Act rather than concentrating solely on sanctions against healthcare professionals.

The Senate Minority Leader, Senator Abba Moro (PDP, Benue South), said the bill had exposed several gaps requiring comprehensive legislative attention.

He expressed confidence that the committee stage and proposed public hearing would provide opportunities for healthcare professionals and other stakeholders to make contributions.

Moro, who cited experiences in Mexico where emergency responders and ambulances reportedly attended promptly to accident victims, condemned the practice of hospitals demanding police reports before treating emergency patients.

He stressed that saving lives should remain the priority in emergency situations.

In his remarks, the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, said the debate had highlighted important challenges requiring attention across the country’s healthcare system.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Akpabio urged lawmakers to support the bill’s progression, noting that identified shortcomings could be addressed through further legislative deliberations and consultations with relevant stakeholders.

He stressed that the Federal Government, state governments and local government authorities must work together to provide the facilities and resources required for effective healthcare delivery.

title: French blood supplies impacted by freezer hacks as theories swirl about culprits
excerpt: French authorities say that fridges used in medical facilities to store blood for donations were impacted by recent cyber-attacks by unknown hackers.
description: French authorities say that fridges used in medical facilities to store blood for donations were impacted by recent cyber-attacks by unknown hackers.
content:
French authorities say that fridges used in medical facilities to store blood for donations were impacted by recent cyber-attacks by unknown hackers.

The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said cold rooms storing blood were impacted by hackers, with temperatures set to rise - but staff intervened to protect blood supplies.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

"No health impact has been identified and no loss of blood products is to be reported," the EFS said.

Up until now, only supermarkets were known to have been impacted by the hacks.

Meanwhile rumours have been circulating online about Russian hacktivist groups claiming they worked together on the waves of freezer hacks which have affected European supermarkets.

Noname057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance reportedly posted on Telegram that they were responsible, bragging that they had "once again demonstrated a high level of skill and precision".

But their posts and channels have now been deleted and the claims are being met with some scepticism.

While Russian groups are not being ruled out, experts say Iranian hacktivists or nation state hackers - or even teenagers pulling pranks - could also be the culprits.

Cyber-security researchers at multiple firms are pouring over evidence gathered from so-called "honeypots" to provide clues as to who is behind the waves of freezer hacks.

Three separate cyber-security firms have deployed fake freezer software traps to monitor how hackers attempt to use them for attacks.

In cyber-security, a "honeypot" is a digital decoy - such as a fake computer network or file - deliberately set up to look like a vulnerable target to lure and trap hackers.

By monitoring these traps, security experts can safely study an attacker's methods without putting real systems at risk.

According to activity gathered after the first wave of cyber-attacks, the second wave which hit several European countries was highly targeted.

"The fact that all these fridge freezers were hit simultaneously suggests planning and coordination," says Ryan Dewhurst from Spanish cyber-security company Previdian.

The entry point to the affected freezer software products was not difficult to exploit as they were poorly protected, with known attack methods already floating around online.

But experts like Dewhurst say the hacker or hackers had to gather the information about the devices' public IP addresses to create a target list then take time to plan which methods to use and when to execute them.

"Given the reported timing of when the devices had their temperatures increased, which seems to have been overnight for maximum damage - this is further evidence that the attack was planned and co-ordinated," he said.

Another cyber firm which has deployed similar honeypot tech to lure the hackers into revealing their tactics is Strathclyde-based Lupovis.

It had honeypots which appeared to be located around the world, and started seeing activity 10 days before the second wave of cyber-attacks.

Intriguingly, the team saw hackers scanning and probing their fake freezer sites only in Europe.

"We saw none of our honeypots in places like Africa or South America targeted at all," said Lupovis founder Dr Xavier Bellekens.

"Even pots in Ukraine were left alone."

A third company - French cyber-defence firm Sekoia - also noticed scanning activity prior to the second wave of cyber-attacks, but said it could have been automatic scanning without malicious intent.

In a report to its customers, it said evidence suggested the nature of the attack aligned with activity of Russian hacktivists or the Russian government, which is being accused of carrying out so-called "hybrid warfare" cyber-attacks across Europe.

But Sekoia's research also points to Iranian regime hackers or hacktivists too.

"Iranian-aligned actors have an established record of targeting internet-exposed industrial control systems and previous incidents involved the same equipment in Israel and the US - both adversaries of Iran," the report said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

According to Sekoia, about 40 Israeli supermarkets running Danfoss controllers were compromised back in 2022.

Meanwhile in late August, freezers in at least six US military bases were forced into defrost mode, as in France. The controller models remain unconfirmed and investigations are ongoing.

In a now deleted post online, NoName and Z-Pentest Alliance claim to have targeted freezer software maker Danfoss since the start of 2026.

"To date, we have no technical evidence indicating the involvement of Russian-speaking groups," a Sekoia spokesperson told the BBC.

"Furthermore, as NoName057 is not known to effectively conduct operations beyond DDoS attacks and has a history of making false attributions, we remain sceptical of their alleged claim of responsibility."

Distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks work by flooding a website or online service with internet traffic in an attempt to throw it offline, or otherwise make it inaccessible.

Authorities in several countries are actively investigating the hacks and warning supermarkets about potential future attacks.

But no formal attribution has been made.

None of the three cyber firms which have been gathering honey pot data are ruling out that it could be a teenager.

But with the degree of planning necessary the experts all agree it would have to be a well co-ordinated group - and if so, they would expect online bragging to surface soon.

Sekoia also said the possibility remains that all three waves could have been carried out by different and distinct groups or copycats.

title: Nigeria-Korea trade hits $1.1bn as both countries seek diversification
excerpt: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja
description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja
content:
By Favour Ulebor, Abuja

The Republic of Korea has expressed its readiness to deepen trade and investment ties with Nigeria, targeting sectors such as manufacturing, agriculture, digital technology and maritime services beyond the traditional oil and gas trade.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The Korean Ambassador to Nigeria, Jeong Yo-an, disclosed this on Wednesday at a meeting with journalists in Abuja, saying expanding economic cooperation would boost bilateral trade, encourage local production and create employment opportunities in both countries.

He said trade between Nigeria and Korea reached approximately $1.1bn last year, making Nigeria one of Korea’s largest trading partners in Africa.

However, the ambassador noted that the existing trade structure, largely dominated by Nigerian oil and gas exports and Korean exports of automobiles, electronics and machinery, needed to become more diversified.

“Last year, our trade reached about 1.1 billion dollars. Nigeria remains one of Korea’s largest trading partners in Africa. But the shape of our trade must change. Today, Nigeria sells us mostly oil and gas. Korea sells mostly cars, electronics and machinery. We can do much more than that,” he said.

Jeong said the next phase of bilateral cooperation would focus on strengthening local production, including vehicle assembly, agricultural machinery for rice farmers, digital skills development and maritime services.

He added that Korea was interested in encouraging more Nigerian businesses to participate in bilateral trade while attracting Korean companies to invest in local manufacturing and other productive sectors.

The ambassador identified the beauty and cosmetics industry as another area offering significant opportunities, citing growing Nigerian interest in Korean skincare and cosmetic products.

According to him, Nigeria’s large youth population presents a considerable market for Korean beauty products and could position the country as a major destination for such products in Africa.

He said the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), through its Lagos office, was available to connect Korean manufacturers with Nigerian importers and help local businesses identify potential buyers in Korea.

Jeong also disclosed that Nigerian buyers would have the opportunity to engage with Korean companies at the Korean pavilion during the Beauty West Africa exhibition scheduled for November 13.

On diplomatic relations, he said both countries were working to strengthen political and economic cooperation following the Korea-Africa Summit in 2024 and the first Korea-Africa Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held in June this year.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He added that Nigeria had offered to host the seventh session of the Nigeria-Korea Joint Commission in Abuja as part of efforts to advance bilateral engagement.

On development cooperation, the ambassador disclosed that approximately 2,000 Nigerian public officials had received training in Korea through the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA).

He said KOICA’s Smart School project had also reached 8,000 pupils and trained more than 300 teachers and school leaders.

According to him, KOICA, the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) had commenced work on the Abuja Centre for Entrepreneurship to support young Nigerians in developing business ideas and creating jobs.

He said Korea was equally supporting initiatives aimed at promoting green jobs, agricultural development, digital education and skills acquisition.

The ambassador further disclosed that Korea was working towards increasing its Official Development Assistance to $10bn by 2030, alongside plans to provide $14bn in export financing to support Korean companies investing in Africa.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

On cultural exchanges, Jeong said the Korean Cultural Centre Nigeria had reached more than 300,000 people through its programmes, while this year’s Korean Film Festival attracted approximately 1,000 participants.

He pledged to extend cultural activities to more Nigerian cities and promote collaborations between young creatives in both countries.

title: ‘We have kissed empty Mondays goodbye’ — Mbah on IPOB sit-at-home in Enugu
excerpt: By Adegboyega Adeleye
description: By Adegboyega Adeleye
content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah says residents have overcome the fear that kept roads and communities quiet on Mondays during the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) sit-at-home campaign, pointing to security measures along key routes in the state.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Mbah spoke at the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign flag-off in Nsukka on Wednesday, saying the change meant people could travel without the fear of attacks that had previously disrupted movement.

“The other thing that reminds me is that we have kissed empty Mondays goodbye. All the challenges we had travelling on that road because of fear of attack, today, we have kissed it goodbye,” he said.

The sit-at-home was initially called by IPOB in 2021 in solidarity with its detained leader, Nnamdi Kanu.

Although the order was later suspended in 2026, fear of attacks continued to keep businesses and public activity subdued on some Mondays.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Mbah said the state deployed its “distress response squad” along the route, rather than setting up roadblocks, and asked residents of Nsukka, Enugu West and Enugu East to watch for changes around them.

“We do not have roadblocks, but we have the watchful eyes of our distress response squad across the entire stretch. So, Nsukka, Ndi Enugu West, Ndi Enugu East, maybe we should even start with Nsukka: what is changing around you?” the governor said.



---

He urged residents to see the area’s development as evidence of transformation.

“Can you just look around and you can see it? This is transformation,” Mbah added.

…Says NELFUND disbursed ₦372.62bn in student loans

ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has disclosed that President Bola Tinubu’s administration has returned over one million out-of-school children to classrooms.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The Council said this in a statement on Wednesday by its Spokesperson, Dele Alake, citing the Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI) 2026 report of the Federal Ministry of Education.

The report credits the Better Education Service Delivery for All (BESDA) programme for the feat. It also says the programme trained 1,400 Tsangaya teachers and set up 200 bilingual centres across 17 northern states.

The Adolescent Girls Initiative for Learning and Empowerment (AGILE) has reached 7.19 million girls, of whom 3.7 million are enrolled in secondary schools. Over 10,000 schools have also benefited from improved facilities, according to the council.

On funding, the Federal Government reportedly allocated a record ₦3.52 trillion to education in the 2026 budget. It also secured $552 million for a basic education programme targeting 29 million children, over 500,000 teachers and 65,000 public schools.

According to the council, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund NELFUND has processed 1,659,853 student loan applications and disbursed ₦372.62 billion. Of this, ₦192.89 billion went to tuition and ₦179.73 billion to upkeep allowances, across 319 tertiary institutions.

The statement said the administration has resolved the age-long dispute with the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) and implemented the agreement providing for a 40 per cent increase in academic staff remuneration and improved welfare benefits.

The Tertiary Institutions Staff Support Fund, it added, has paid out ₦28 billion to 15,000 workers in 153 public institutions. Eligible staff can access loans of up to ₦10 million for housing, healthcare, transportation and education.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

On technical and vocational education and training (TVET), the scheme has drawn over 2.8 million applications. A total of 156,446 verified trainees are receiving free training, monthly stipends and start-up support.

Alake said more than ₦65.7 billion has been disbursed to trainees and ₦30.2 billion to training centres. Thirty-eight technical colleges have been rehabilitated, and technical education now covers tuition, boarding, textbooks and uniforms at no cost to students.

On teacher development, Alake said 53,553 teachers have registered under EduRevamp, and 51,794 have joined the first cohort of the Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway (ATPP). The six-month programme offers professional qualifications, certification and licensing. Backed by ₦2 billion, it targets 250,000 teachers by 2027, he added.

Alake added that in medical education, ₦110 billion is going into rehabilitating 18 federal medical schools across the six geopolitical zones. Nursing enrolment rose from 81,480 in 2023 to 114,300 in 2025. Twenty science, technology, engineering and medical sciences institutions have been approved, and 12 engineering and technology faculties are targeted for rehabilitation.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, said the success of the reforms would be judged by their impact on students, teachers and institutions, not by the money allocated or the number of programmes introduced.

“Our measure of success is not merely the amount of money allocated to education or the number of programmes introduced. It is the difference these interventions make in the lives of our children, students, teachers and institutions,” he said.

title: 2027: Makinde proposes minimum 51% threshold for presidential victory
excerpt: …rules out personal benefit from proposed constitutional changes, backs transitional government
description: …rules out personal benefit from proposed constitutional changes, backs transitional government
content:
…rules out personal benefit from proposed constitutional changes, backs transitional government

By Soni Daniel & Luminous Jannamike

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

ABUJA — Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, on Wednesday proposed a minimum 50 per cent-plus-one vote threshold for presidential elections, saying Nigeria needs a political system that compels presidential candidates to secure broader national support before assuming office.

Makinde, who unveiled the Reset Nigeria Manifesto in Abuja, also declared that he would not personally benefit from any constitutional and political arrangements that might emerge from his proposed transitional government, insisting that the process must not be manipulated to serve the interests of its promoters.

He said the proposed electoral threshold would encourage political parties to build alliances across ethnic, religious and regional divisions, while a transitional government would provide a platform for Nigerians to negotiate a new political and constitutional direction.

Offering himself as a test of his commitment to the proposed reforms, Makinde said: “Today, Wednesday, November 4, 2026, I offer myself as a guinea pig by announcing to Nigerians that whatever constitutional and political arrangements we eventually develop, I will not be a beneficiary.

“If I intend to benefit personally from the arrangements, there is a possibility that manipulation could set in. But I do not want that to happen.”

Explaining the proposed presidential election threshold, the governor argued that candidates should secure sufficient national support to command the respect of the majority rather than emerge through an electoral arrangement that leaves most voters behind.

“What we are proposing is that, to become President of Nigeria, a candidate must secure at least 50 per cent plus one vote,” Makinde said.

“That way, candidates and political parties will have to engage in discussions across party lines and other divisions to secure the support needed to form a government that commands the respect of the majority of Nigerians.”

He identified four fundamental concerns behind his Reset Agenda: the prioritisation of macroeconomic reforms over broad-based economic growth; failure by governments to accept responsibility for results; weak institutions undermined by divisions and bribery; and the exclusion of millions of poor Nigerians from government decisions.

Makinde criticised the emphasis on macroeconomic reforms without corresponding improvements in the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians, insisting that economic stability must translate into affordable food, employment, improved incomes and a lower cost of living.

“My simple proposition is that government must make life easier for the people. That is all,” he said.

Questioning the value of economic stability that does not improve household welfare, he added: “What does macroeconomic stability mean if it does not improve the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians?”

The governor identified high energy costs as one of the structural problems undermining Nigerian businesses, particularly manufacturers dependent on diesel-powered generators.

“For instance, no matter how hard I try, a manufacturer who relies on generators powered by diesel will continue to incur high production costs. We must make it possible for manufacturers to connect to the national electricity grid and access electricity at a lower cost,” he said.

He also questioned how the country was managing increased crude oil revenues, arguing that rising international oil prices should produce measurable benefits for Nigerians rather than simply increase government allocations.

Makinde, who said he had spent much of his working life in the oil and gas industry, recalled his personal journey from Ibadan to Port-Harcourt in search of opportunities in 1990.

“I left Ibadan in early October 1990 with just a bag containing a few belongings, perhaps two pairs of trousers, three or four shirts and a book. The only thing I had was the fare to travel to Kaduna with my degree,” he recalled.

He said he eventually secured employment, established a business, raised a family and built his life, experiences that informed his conviction that government policies must create opportunities for ordinary Nigerians.

On accountability, Makinde promised that his proposed administration would establish measurable performance targets within its first 100 days and make its achievements subject to public scrutiny.

He also faulted the Federal Government’s handling of the electricity sector, arguing that the transfer of regulatory powers to states should not become an excuse for abandoning national responsibilities.

“Yes, but should a baby that has just been born start crawling, walking and running at the same time?” he asked.

He maintained that while states should develop their electricity markets according to their capacities, the Federal Government must continue to manage national electricity assets and address challenges affecting generation and distribution.

Makinde further called for continuity in national development policies irrespective of changes in political parties, citing the succession of different administrations in Oyo State since 1999.

“Political parties will come and go, but our national development plans and the things we must do for our people must remain constant. We must continue to implement them, irrespective of the political party in power,” he said.

On petroleum pricing, he questioned the argument that lower fuel prices in Nigeria would encourage smuggling into neighbouring countries, insisting that the government should strengthen border management rather than transfer the consequences of enforcement failures to citizens.

He also advocated a new social and political order in which institutions would function across party and regional differences, adding that more than half of Nigeria’s population lived in poverty and should not be treated as an afterthought in government decisions.

Makinde said the Reset Agenda was developed through extensive consultations and town hall meetings across the six geopolitical zones, where Nigerians were asked to articulate their expectations of government.

He recalled that some participants had challenged him to provide the kind of leadership associated with Nigeria’s founding fathers, including Tafawa Balewa, Obafemi Awolowo and Nnamdi Azikiwe.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Earlier, the APM vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, called for a national conference involving government representatives and all segments of Nigerian society to resolve the country’s longstanding political contradictions.

Daura, who described the first government under their proposed arrangement as transitional, said the process would allow Nigerians to discuss their differences, reach agreements and establish a common direction for the country.

He warned against attempts by governments to weaken opposition parties, arguing that effective opposition was necessary for political stability and democratic development.

“The opposition is complementary to the government; it is not an enemy of the government,” he said.

Daura maintained that the suppression of political opponents and denial of a level playing field ultimately threatened the country and its citizens.

He said opposition parties should be allowed to participate freely in the political process, adding that the quality of opposition could help reduce political tension and strengthen democratic institutions.

Also speaking, National Chairman of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Yusuf Dantalle, warned against attempts to use state institutions to undermine democratic competition, urging political leaders to protect the country’s democratic institutions.

Dantalle questioned the gap between the promises made by the governing All Progressives Congress, APC, during its election campaigns and the economic realities Nigerians were currently facing.

He criticised rising petroleum prices and the burden of taxation on citizens and businesses, arguing that the country’s economic difficulties required urgent attention.

The APM chairman also urged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to discharge its responsibilities impartially and ensure that electoral activities were conducted in an atmosphere of peace.

He warned that electoral fraud amounted to a denial of citizens’ democratic rights because it deprived them of the opportunity to choose their leaders.

Dantalle said the younger generation was looking up to political leaders to protect the country’s democratic future and called for collective efforts to prevent the weakening of democratic institutions.

In his remarks, National Chairman of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, described Makinde as a leading figure in the opposition, recalling how he won the 2019 Oyo governorship election on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, despite the dominance of the APC in the South-West at the time.

Gombe also praised Makinde and Bauchi State Governor, Bala Mohammed, for sustaining opposition cooperation, saying their efforts had helped rekindle democratic engagement among political parties.

He recalled that when the SDP struggled to secure a venue for its convention in Abuja, it eventually approached Mohammed, who offered Bauchi State as an alternative venue.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

Gombe said Makinde also hosted an initiative that brought opposition political parties together, adding that the engagement had encouraged further consultations among political leaders and presidential aspirants.

He urged opposition leaders to embrace humility, patriotism and cooperation in their efforts to strengthen democracy.

title: Army kills three suspected kidnappers in Kogi shootout

content:
Troops of the 12 Composite Brigade of the Nigerian Army have killed three suspected kidnappers during a gun battle in Igalamela/Odolu Local Government Area of Kogi State.

The troops, operating alongside personnel of the Kogi State Vigilance Service (KSVS), also recovered four AK-47 rifles and a cache of ammunition during a follow-up operation.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The Brigade’s spokesman, Lieutenant Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement, saying the operation was conducted on November 4, 2026, as part of efforts to dismantle kidnapping networks operating in the area.

He said the operation followed earlier raids and exploitation activities in Edimogbo Forest, where suspected kidnappers were believed to be operating.

According to him, the joint security team extended its search from Edimogbo Forest towards Obele Forest in pursuit of fleeing suspects.

“During the operation, troops made contact with the suspected kidnappers, who attempted to escape upon sighting the security forces.

“The encounter resulted in the neutralisation of three suspected kidnappers, while subsequent exploitation of the area led to the recovery of four AK-47 rifles, 12 magazines, 336 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, three bandoliers and an identity card,” he said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Abdullahi said the operation was part of sustained efforts to deny criminal elements freedom of movement and dismantle their hideouts through offensive operations and intelligence-driven patrols.

He added that maintaining security dominance in the area would help restore confidence among residents of affected communities.

The Commander of the 12 Composite Brigade, Brigadier General Kasim Umar Sidi, commended the troops and personnel of the Kogi State Vigilance Service for their resilience and professionalism.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He urged them to sustain the momentum and remain vigilant to prevent criminal elements from establishing safe havens within the brigade’s area of responsibility.

The Nigerian Army reaffirmed its commitment to protecting lives and property in Kogi State and neighbouring areas, urging residents to provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing operations.

content:
INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌⁠‌‍⁠⁠‍​‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance on Wednesday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by the British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Mr Pete Vowles, to INEC headquarters.

Amupitan noted that restoring public trust, enhancing operational efficiency and safeguarding the integrity of every ballot remained the central pillars of his administration.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

“Your arrival comes at a defining period in our national journey, as Nigeria deepens its democratic processes and advances institutional reforms ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“We view your visit today as a continuation of the enduring partnership and shared commitment to democratic integrity that exists between Nigeria and the United Kingdom,” he said.

Acknowledging the United Kingdom’s long-standing support through the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and development partners, Amupitan called for expanded strategic collaboration in critical areas as 2027 approaches.

He listed priority partnership areas to include election cybersecurity architecture, specialised capacity building for the commission’s personnel and joint initiatives to counter artificial intelligence-driven manipulation, disinformation and foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI).

“The integrity of Nigeria’s democracy matters not only to our citizens but to the peace, stability and economic growth of the entire West African sub-region and the African continent.

“We assure you and the international community that INEC remains resolutely independent, impartial and committed to delivering a 2027 general election that meets the highest global standards,” Amupitan said.

Reviewing recent electoral activities, the INEC cited the successful conduct of off-cycle governorship elections in Anambra, Ekiti and Osun states, alongside the FCT Area Council polls and 16 state and federal legislative by-elections.

He explained that the off-cycle polls served as operational testing grounds, recording major advancements in early logistics deployment and high Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) reliability.

Amupitan said that the elections also witnessed swift uploading of polling unit results on the INEC Result Viewing (IReV) portal as well as priority voting access for persons with disabilities (PWDs), pregnant women and the elderly.

He said that with over 70 days to the 2027 general elections, the commission had successfully executed nine out of the 14 key activities outlined in its revised timetable and schedule of activities.

To ensure that every registered voter exercised their franchise, Amupitan said that INEC had launched an intensive permanent voter card (PVC) collection drive, decentralised across all the 774 local government areas down to the ward registration level.

He also emphasised measures taken to protect candidate nominations under Section 29 of the Electoral Act 2026 through the INEC Candidates Nomination Portal (ICNP).

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He disclosed that the platform successfully processed nominations across 21 registered political parties, encompassing 36 presidential and vice-presidential candidates from 18 parties, 4,860 National Assembly candidates, 936 governorship candidates and 9,692 state assembly candidates.

On technical infrastructure, the INEC boss revealed that the commission had secured 57,000 new BVAS devices.

He added that comprehensive zonal physical and operational assessments were ongoing, with the South-South evaluation concluded and the North-Central assessment scheduled to commence on Thursday.

In his remarks, the high commissioner, who said that he had been in Nigeria for eight weeks, noted that the courtesy visit was primarily to familiarise himself with INEC’s operations and the preparations for the elections.

Vowles underscored the importance of Nigeria’s democracy to its citizens, the West African sub-region and the international community, describing the forthcoming elections as an important opportunity for Nigeria to demonstrate how a strong democracy could function in a large and diverse country.

“The reason I suppose that we wanted a courtesy call is perhaps an obvious one, but just the recognition of how much Nigeria’s democracy matters to Nigeria, to 240 million Nigerians, to the region and to the world.

“I guess as a foreigner in your country, recognising the importance of Nigeria’s democracy globally is such an important thing.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

“So, I wanted to recognise that, and the opportunity to understand the operations and the preparations for Nigeria’s elections.

“I would probably say that in our conversation, we talked about how the forthcoming elections are a really important opportunity for Nigeria to showcase to the world how a strong democracy in a large, diverse country should operate. (NAN)

title: Okpebholo, Oba of Benin pledge support for NDLEA drug war
excerpt: BENIN CITY — Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, and the Oba of Benin, Oba Ewuare II, have pledged support for the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) in its ...
description: BENIN CITY — Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, and the Oba of Benin, Oba Ewuare II, have pledged support for the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) in its ...
content:
BENIN CITY — Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, and the Oba of Benin, Oba Ewuare II, have pledged support for the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) in its campaign against substance abuse and illicit drug trafficking.

The two leaders gave the assurance on Wednesday when the NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), led the agency’s War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) advocacy campaign to Benin City.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Receiving Marwa and his delegation at the Government House, Okpebholo described the fight against illicit drugs as a collective responsibility, noting that substance abuse was associated with several criminal activities.

The governor, who said he had admired Marwa since his secondary school days, commended the NDLEA command in Edo State and pledged his administration’s support for its operations.

“There is the need for everyone to get involved and support the fight against substance abuse and illicit drug trafficking, because at the root of virtually every crime is the issue of drugs.

“From our experience, even kidnappers first ask their victims for drugs before demanding ransom. That shows that illicit drug is our enemy,” he said.

Okpebholo added: “Your officers and men in Edo are doing excellent work. We are ready to work with you, we are ready to partner with you, and we are ready to support you with any request you bring before us.”

In his remarks, Marwa commended the governor’s support for the agency and sought his cooperation in implementing the NDLEA’s Alternative Development Programme, which encourages cannabis growers to switch to legitimate crops and sustainable livelihoods.

He explained that the initiative, introduced last year, was designed to discourage illicit cannabis cultivation by providing farmers with alternatives and support for legitimate agricultural activities.

According to him, the pilot phase of the programme, launched in Ondo State in January, had recorded encouraging results, prompting the agency to extend it to Edo.

Marwa sought the governor’s support for the programme, as well as additional logistics assistance for NDLEA operations in the state.

The highlight of the visit was the decoration of Okpebholo as a WADA Grand Ambassador in recognition of his support for the campaign against substance abuse and illicit drug trafficking.

Marwa and his delegation subsequently visited the Oba of Benin at his palace, where the NDLEA chairman described drug abuse as one of the major challenges confronting Nigeria.

He disclosed that more than 15 million Nigerians were involved in drug abuse, representing a prevalence rate about three times the global average.

Marwa said the problem had spread to schools and communities across the country, including the Benin Kingdom.

He also disclosed that the agency arrested more than 1,200 suspected drug traffickers and seized over 30 tonnes of illicit substances in Edo State in 2025.

He added that of the 16 million kilogrammes of assorted illicit substances seized nationwide by the agency in the last five years, cannabis accounted for about 75 per cent.

According to him, Edo is among the states where cannabis is cultivated.

Marwa said the NDLEA’s responsibilities extended beyond enforcing drug laws to providing counselling, treatment and rehabilitation for people struggling with substance dependence.

“It is the job of the NDLEA to enforce the law against drug trafficking, and as well help those who are addicted to drugs with counselling, treatment and rehabilitation.

“But this is an assignment that we cannot do alone. It is a whole-of-society approach. We need the traditional institutions, the church, CSOs, government and the media, because all hands must be on deck,” he said.

He particularly emphasised the importance of traditional institutions, describing them as influential partners in community mobilisation against drug abuse.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

The NDLEA chairman acknowledged the Oba’s support in tackling drug abuse and other social problems, including kidnapping and human trafficking.

He appealed to the monarch to encourage communities across the Benin Kingdom to shun illicit drug cultivation and trafficking and support the Alternative Development Programme.

Explaining the initiative, Marwa said Nigeria was the first country in Africa to adopt alternative development as a strategic pillar of drug control, an approach welcomed by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and endorsed by the Federal Government.

Under the programme, cannabis growers are encouraged to cultivate legitimate crops such as cassava, yam and maize, with support from the Federal Government, state governments and the NDLEA.

The support includes farm inputs and community infrastructure such as roads, schools, clinics and water supply.

Marwa said some farmers had expressed appreciation for the initiative because it offered them an opportunity to pursue legitimate farming without fear of arrest over illicit cannabis cultivation.

Responding, the Oba of Benin thanked the NDLEA chairman for the visit and recognition of the kingdom’s efforts in tackling drug abuse.

He said: “Thank you very much for recognising the work of Benin, the people and the culture of the people, and also the efforts we have been making to fight the scourge of drug abuse.”

The monarch also disclosed that he had suggestions for improving the agency’s operations, which he intended to forward privately to the NDLEA chairman.

As part of the WADA advocacy campaign in Edo, Marwa also met with leaders of the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW) in the state, led by Comrade Saturday Oamen.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

He urged the union to use its platforms and influence to sensitise members against drug abuse and trafficking and partner with the NDLEA to keep roads, motor parks and communities free of illicit substances.

Marwa was also scheduled to meet religious and civil society leaders as part of the campaign.

---

He urged the people of Imo State to support Uzodimma, whom he described as a politician with considerable influence and mobilisation capacity in the South-East.

“This is the best way to deliver the President come January 2027, and his efforts and commitment have never been in doubt. I would equally call on the President to urgently intervene in this matter.

“This is because the achievements of Governor Uzodimma speak volumes and, as an achiever, he is following the commendable footsteps of President Tinubu towards making Nigeria a better place to live,” he said.

Onyekwere also called on the people of Abia State to support the APC governorship candidate, Eric Opia, whom he described as young and vibrant.

He urged APC members in the South-East to close ranks and work towards strengthening the party’s electoral fortunes in the region.

He expressed confidence that the South-East would benefit from supporting Tinubu and politicians in the region working towards his re-election.

title: Lagos Opens Legal Research Centre, Targets Stronger Justice Delivery
excerpt: The Lagos State Government has opened a Centre for Legal Study, Research and Training, describing it as a strategic investment to strengthen the justice system, develop legal ex...
description: The Lagos State Government has opened a Centre for Legal Study, Research and Training, describing it as a strategic investment to strengthen the justice system, develop legal ex...
content:
The Lagos State Government has opened a Centre for Legal Study, Research and Training, describing it as a strategic investment to strengthen the justice system, develop legal expertise and prepare the state’s justice institutions for emerging challenges.

Established by the Lagos State Ministry of Justice, the Centre is expected to serve as a hub for legal research, professional training, policy development and capacity building for practitioners and public officials in the justice sector.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Speaking at the official opening ceremony in Alausa, Ikeja, on Wednesday, the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Lawal Pedro, SAN, described the facility as more than another government building, saying it represents a deliberate investment in knowledge, institutional excellence and the future of justice administration in Lagos State.

“There are occasions when we open a building or office. There are other occasions when we open a door to the future. Today, in Lagos, we are doing the latter — opening a door to the future,” Pedro said.

He described the Centre as the first of its kind within a Ministry of Justice in Nigeria, arguing that a justice system that intends to remain relevant and effective must continually educate, examine and reform itself.

Pedro said the initiative aligns with the broader development agenda of the Sanwo-Olu administration, noting that the development of Lagos cannot be separated from strong institutions and an efficient administration of justice.

He identified the rule of law, access to justice and capable institutions as essential foundations for economic development, good governance and social inclusion.

The Attorney-General also linked the Centre to the administration’s THEMES Plus Agenda, stressing that building a secure, economically vibrant and inclusive society requires sustained investment in the people and institutions responsible for interpreting, administering and developing the state’s laws.

He said the Centre would help address the growing demands of a modern justice system, including the need for continuous professional development, evidence-based policy and institutional reform.

Outlining its proposed operational framework, Pedro disclosed that the Ministry intends to incorporate the Centre as a not-for-profit entity under a public-private partnership arrangement.

Under the proposed structure, the Ministry of Justice and its private-sector partners will jointly manage the Centre’s day-to-day operations.

While the government will provide policy direction, legitimacy and strategic oversight, the private sector is expected to contribute funding, technical expertise, innovation and operational efficiency.

Pedro said the arrangement was designed to ensure the Centre’s sustainability and effectiveness.

The opening ceremony also provided an opportunity to recognise former Attorneys-General and Commissioners for Justice, as well as past Solicitors-General and Permanent Secretaries whose contributions helped shape the Lagos State Ministry of Justice.

Pedro said their names had been inscribed on a Roll of Honour at the entrance to the Centre in recognition of their service, vision and enduring contributions.

He said the establishment of the facility reflected the importance of honouring the past, strengthening the present and investing in the future of the state’s justice system.

The Attorney-General commended Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu for providing the leadership under which the initiative was realised, noting that the project was initially conceived as part of a broader commitment to institutional development.

The Governor was represented at the ceremony by the Secretary to the State Government, Bimbola Salu-Hundeyin.

Other guests included a former President of the Nigerian Bar Association, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN; former Lagos State Attorneys-General, Mrs Eniola Fadayomi, Wonuola Folami and Adeniji Kazeem, SAN; as well as Senior Advocates Femi Falana, Bimbo Akeredolu and Jelili Owonikoko.

Also in attendance were judges of the Lagos State Judiciary, the chairmen of NBA branches in Lagos and representatives of the state executive and legislature.

Pedro expressed appreciation to the judiciary, members of the Nigerian Bar Association, development partners and the Ministry’s workforce for their contributions to the justice sector.

He said the Centre should ultimately become a platform for producing better-informed legal professio

nals, strengthening public institutions and advancing reforms to improve the administration of justice in Lagos State.

He called on stakeholders to see the facility not as an isolated government project but as part of a wider vision of a Greater Lagos, where strong institutions, developed human capital and respect for the rule of law underpin sustainable progress.

Pedro formally welcomed guests to the Centre, describing it as a legacy investment whose significance would become increasingly evident with time.

Meanwhile, Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Femi Falana, has urged the Lagos State Ministry of Justice to make the Centre a repository of Nigeria’s legal history and a platform for promoting compliance with court judgments.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Citing the landmark Privy Council decision in Amodu Tijani v. Secretary, Southern Nigeria (1921), Falana challenged misconceptions surrounding land ownership in Lagos, recalling that the judgment recognised existing indigenous proprietary and usufructuary rights.

He urged the Ministry to preserve landmark judgments and historical legal materials at the Centre to deepen legal scholarship and provide researchers with access to important legal authorities.

Falana also called on Pedro to sustain efforts to secure compliance with outstanding court judgments, while encouraging the Ministry to explore settlements in appropriate cases rather than prolonging litigation.

He further advocated the inclusion of customary courts in the Centre’s research and training programmes.

According to him, judicial reforms since 1999 have largely concentrated on superior courts of record, leaving customary courts, which serve a significant proportion of the population, without comparable attention.

He urged the Ministry to dedicate a section of the Centre to customary law and the administration of justice at that level.

Also speaking at the ceremony, the Solicitor-General and Permanent Secretary of the Lagos State Ministry of Justice, Hameed Oyenuga, disclosed that the Ministry’s management had resolved to approach Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu to name the newly established Centre after Pedro in recognition of his decades of service and contributions to the state’s justice sector.

Oyenuga described the proposed recognition as a tribute to Pedro’s professional accomplishments and his place in the institutional history of the Ministry.

He recalled that Pedro joined the Lagos State Ministry of Justice in December 1987 and served in several directorates before rising through the ranks to become Solicitor-General and Permanent Secretary in 2008.

In the same year, Pedro attained the rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria, becoming, according to Oyenuga, the first State Counsel in the Lagos State public service to achieve the distinction.

His career spanned civil litigation, public prosecution and the development of the state’s justice administration framework before his appointment as Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice in September 2023.

“The intention is not merely to attach a distinguished name to a building. It is to recognise a record of service and create a lasting association between professional excellence, institutional development and the advancement of justice,” Oyenuga said.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

The Centre marks a new institutional initiative by the Lagos State Ministry of Justice, with its long-term impact expected to depend on the strength of its governance structure, research output, professional training programmes and ability to preserve legal knowledge for future generations.

Kidnappers have released a man and five other mourners who were abducted while conveying his wife’s corpse for burial in Benue State, following the reported payment of N2.5m ransom.

The six victims were kidnapped around 8pm on Friday along Adoka Road in Otukpo Local Government Area while travelling to Okpoga in Okpokwu LGA.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

The deceased woman reportedly died in Kano, and her husband and five others were transporting her remains for burial when gunmen intercepted their vehicle along the road.

The kidnappers reportedly abandoned the corpse on the highway and demanded N15m ransom for the release of the victims.

A source told our correspondent that the six abductees regained their freedom in the early hours of Wednesday after their families paid N2.5m.

“The six kidnap victims were released early hours of today after family paid N2.5 million,” the source said.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

Confirming their release, the Chairman of Otukpo Local Government Area, Maxwell Ogiri, said the victims were freed between Tuesday night and Wednesday morning but declined to comment on the ransom payment.

“It’s true that the victims were released between Tuesday night and the early hours of Wednesday,” he said.



---

### 🎙️ Perspectives & What Comes Next

However, the Police Public Relations Officer in the state, DSP Peter Aondongu, said he was yet to receive confirmation of their release.

“I am yet to get the report of the release of the kidnap victims,” the police spokesman said.

title: ‘I want justice,’ says slain Ghanaian teen’s mother

content:
The mother of a 15-year-old Ghanaian boy, Javits Frimpong, who was fatally shot in the Bronx, New York, has travelled to the United States after receiving an emergency visa approved by President Donald Trump.

The mother, Doris Adu Gyamfi, said she was travelling to America to make arrangements for her son’s funeral and seek justice over his killing.

---

### 📰 The Full Developing Story & Context

Speaking with the BBC on Wednesday at the airport before her departure, Gyamfi said, “I want justice for my son.”

She disclosed that her son had always dreamt of becoming a medical doctor before his life was cut short in the shooting.

Frimpong, who had been in the United States for only a year, was reportedly chased and shot on Thursday morning while on his way to school in the Bronx.

He was rushed to a nearby hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

Police have yet to make any arrests, while investigations are ongoing. Authorities are searching for three teenage boys suspected to have been involved in the killing.

Gyamfi, who was escorted to the airport by relatives and the Head of Mission of the African Diaspora Forum, Dr Erieka Bennett, said her immediate priority was to arrange her son’s burial.

“I’m going to America to plan my son’s funeral,” she said.

She also expressed appreciation to the Ghanaian government and well-wishers for their support, prayers and assistance following the tragedy.

The emergency visa was granted after New York City Mayor, Zohran Mamdani, contacted Trump over the mother’s inability to travel to the United States to mourn her son in person.

In a social media post on Saturday, Mamdani disclosed that Trump had agreed to approve the visa immediately.

He said, “The murder of a child is a pain no parent should endure, let alone from thousands of miles away.”

“Javits Frimpong’s mother deserves to say goodbye to her son in person. I just got off the phone with President Trump, and he has agreed to grant her visa immediately,” Mamdani added.

---

### 🔍 Background, Statements & Official Perspectives

He further said, “All of New York City is mourning this tragedy.”

Meanwhile, the Ghanaian government has condemned the killing and expressed concern over the circumstances surrounding the teenager’s death.

The government said it was closely monitoring the investigation and had urged US authorities to conduct a thorough probe to ensure that those responsible were brought to justice.

It also pledged to provide the necessary legal and consular assistance to the bereaved family.

The killing has sparked outrage in Ghana and the United States, with concerns raised over gun violence and the safety of young people, particularly Ghanaian children sent abroad for education.

The search for the three teenage suspects is ongoing, with police reportedly relying on surveillance footage captured around the scene of the shooting.



---
